sober.name: Sober / Baseline
sober.sleep_strategy: Normal sleep cycle recommended. 9–10 hours pre-event banking.

essential.short: Sleep banking: 9–10 hours per night for days prior.
essential.detail: Banking extra sleep beforehand ("prophylactic sleep extension") appears to build some reserve against the cognitive decline, slowed reaction times, and mood dips that come from staying up past your normal sleep window. The evidence is promising rather than fully settled, but there is no downside to arriving well-rested.

essential.short: Nutrition: Complex carbohydrates + lean protein, 2–4 hours before.
essential.detail: Muscles rely heavily on glycogen during moderate-to-high-intensity activity. Whole grains, brown rice, or quinoa paired with lean proteins ensure gastric emptying is complete before vigorous movement, preventing GI distress while maximizing stored energy.

bonus.short: Hydration: Begin hydrating steadily in advance.
bonus.detail: Avoid drinking large volumes at once. Steady sipping hydrates cells better than rapid intake.

bonus.short: Nap: Consider a 20–90 minute afternoon nap.
bonus.detail: An early-afternoon nap adds to your sleep reserve. Late naps are the ones that push back sleep onset, so nap early if you still plan to sleep that night.

essential.short: Hydration: Drink to thirst, with electrolytes. Do not force extra water down.
essential.detail: You can lose roughly 500 to 1500 mg of sodium an hour in sweat, more if you sweat heavily. The dangerous failure here is the opposite of dehydration: drinking more fluid than you sweat out dilutes your blood sodium and causes exertional hyponatremia, which can be fatal. The early signs are vague: nausea, vomiting, dizziness, headache and puffiness from held fluid. Confusion, seizures and coma come later and mean call an ambulance now. Sports drinks do not prevent it, because they are also dilute. Drinking to thirst does. Electrolytes still help with cramping and general recovery.

sources.label: Hew-Butler et al. 2015: 3rd International Exercise-Associated Hyponatremia Consensus
Baker et al. 2019: normative sweating rate and sweat sodium loss in athletes

essential.short: Heat: Take cool breaks and step out of the crowd before you feel unwell.
essential.detail: Hours of dancing in a hot, dense crowd loads your body faster than it can shed heat. Warning signs are cramping, nausea, dizziness and a pounding headache. Do not wait for sweating to stop: in exertional heat stroke people are usually still sweating heavily. Confusion or a stumbling walk in a hot person is heat stroke, which is a medical emergency: cool them fast and call for help.

essential.short: Nutrition: Simple carbohydrates (fruit, applesauce) for rapid energy.
essential.detail: During vigorous activity, blood is diverted away from the GI tract toward muscles and skin. Fruits provide rapid glucose directly to working muscles without overburdening digestion.

bonus.short: Avoid high-fat or heavy protein foods during activity.
bonus.detail: Dietary fats require prolonged digestion. Forcing the stomach to process heavy foods during exercise leads to bloating, nausea, and cramping due to reduced GI blood flow.

essential.short: Hydration: Rehydrate with electrolytes.
essential.detail: Replace fluid and sodium lost during the event. A balanced electrolyte drink restores blood plasma volume and cellular hydration more effectively than plain water.

bonus.short: Recovery meal: Slow-digesting protein (casein/yogurt) + complex carbohydrates.
bonus.detail: 20 to 40 g of slow protein such as casein before sleep gives a steady supply of amino acids for overnight muscle repair. Carbohydrate is what helps tryptophan reach the brain, where it becomes serotonin and then melatonin; protein works against that step, so expect the sleep benefit to be small.

sources.label: Fernstrom & Wurtman 1971: brain serotonin content after a carbohydrate diet

bonus.short: Supplements: Consider magnesium 1–2 hours before bed.
bonus.detail: Magnesium relaxes muscle by acting as a calcium antagonist at the neuromuscular junction. In the brain it blocks the NMDA receptor and mildly boosts GABA, which calms nerve activity. Sleep trials are small and low quality, so expect a modest effect at best.

sources.label: Mah & Pitre 2021: oral magnesium for insomnia, systematic review

essential.short: Wake up: Expose eyes to natural sunlight promptly.
essential.detail: Morning light is what re-anchors your body clock, because light reaching the eye is the main signal that sets it. Grogginess comes mostly from being woken out of deep sleep, which is more likely after a short night. If you do sleep in, get daylight on your eyes as soon as you are up.

bonus.short: Nutrition: High-protein breakfast + complex carbohydrates.
bonus.detail: Blood glucose swings after sleep deprivation. Eggs on whole-grain toast steady it. Drink 500 ml of water before coffee, because caffeine masks fatigue and acts as a mild diuretic.

bonus.short: Nap: 20–30 minutes before 3 PM if needed.
bonus.detail: A short nap reduces sleep pressure and restores alertness without entering deep slow-wave sleep. Waking from deep sleep during the day causes significant grogginess.

risks: Overheating and heat exhaustion from hours of dancing in a hot, crowded room
Exercise-associated hyponatremia from drinking more than you sweat out
Exhaustion from prolonged exertion
Dehydration and electrolyte imbalance
Sleep deprivation and circadian disruption
sober.visualizer_note: Baseline physical strain only, with no drug toxicity. The real risks of a long night are overheating, fluid balance in both directions, and sleep loss.

alcohol.name: Alcohol

Oral.note: One standard drink is about 10 g of ethanol: a 0.25 L beer at 5 percent, a 0.1 L glass of wine at 12 percent or a 0.03 L shot of 40 percent spirits. This is the EU and WHO convention. A US standard drink is about 14 g.

alcohol.sleep_strategy: Expect fragmented sleep. Hydrate before bed.

essential.short: Meal: Eat a substantial meal with fat and protein before drinking.
essential.detail: Alcohol absorption depends heavily on stomach contents. On an empty stomach the drink passes quickly into the small intestine, where most alcohol is absorbed, producing a sharp blood alcohol spike. Fat and protein slow the stomach emptying, which flattens that spike.

bonus.short: Hydration: Pre-hydrate to offset diuretic effects.
bonus.detail: Alcohol inhibits ADH (antidiuretic hormone), causing extra water loss through the kidneys while your blood alcohol is rising. Starting well-hydrated provides a buffer against that fluid loss.

essential.short: Hydration: Alternating each alcoholic drink with water or an electrolyte drink helps offset dehydration.
essential.detail: Alcohol suppresses ADH secretion, causing the kidneys to pass more water while your blood alcohol is rising. Combined with sweating, this creates rapid two-front fluid loss. Roughly one water per drink is an easy way to limit it.

essential.short: ⚠️ Do not mix with other depressants (ketamine, GHB, benzodiazepines).
essential.detail: Combining CNS depressants amplifies respiratory depression, causes profound motor control loss, and severely increases the risk of unconsciousness. If vomiting occurs while unconscious, the suppressed gag reflex makes aspiration likely.

bonus.short: Note: Alcohol suppresses ADH, causing significant fluid loss.
bonus.detail: With less ADH the kidneys hold back less water, mainly while your blood alcohol is rising, so the effect is short-lived rather than continuous. One small trial in resting men found beer close to fluid-neutral and spirits mildly diuretic, but that is weak evidence and it does not carry over to a hot dance floor where sweat dominates. Do not count beer as hydration, and keep water in the mix.

essential.short: Hydration: A glass or two of water before bed.
essential.detail: Fluids before bed ease next-day thirst, dry mouth and dizziness. They do not prevent the hangover itself: hangover severity does not track electrolyte levels, and drinking water does not prevent or relieve it.

sources.label: Penning et al. 2010: The pathology of alcohol hangover
Mackus et al. 2024: alcohol hangover versus dehydration revisited

essential.short: Position: Sleep on your side if intoxicated.
essential.detail: The recovery position lowers the risk of choking on vomit, which can kill. It does not fix alcohol poisoning. If someone cannot be woken, is breathing slowly or irregularly, or looks cold, clammy or blue, call emergency services. Never leave someone to sleep it off alone.

sources.label: Drugchecking Berlin: First Aid / Erste Hilfe

bonus.short: Food: Skip pre-bed food if nauseous.
bonus.detail: If highly intoxicated, the risk of nocturnal vomiting and aspiration outweighs the benefits of eating. Focus entirely on hydration and safe sleep position instead.

essential.short: Recovery: Eat and drink normally. Skip the vitamin and electrolyte cures.
essential.detail: Thiamine (B1) loss comes from long-term heavy drinking, not from one night out. A hangover is driven mainly by acetaldehyde and inflammation, so vitamins do not undo it. Reviews of hangover cures found no reliable evidence for B vitamins. Eat and drink normally instead.

sources.label: Roberts et al. 2022: interventions for alcohol hangover, systematic review (Addiction)

essential.short: Food: Light, easily digestible foods (toast, eggs).
essential.detail: The gastric mucosa is irritated from alcohol exposure. Light foods provide necessary glucose and amino acids without further irritating the stomach lining.

bonus.short: Avoid: drinking more alcohol to offset a hangover only delays it.
bonus.detail: Consuming more alcohol merely delays the hangover by re-introducing the depressant. It prolongs liver stress, deepens dehydration, and significantly worsens the eventual recovery.

risks: Alcohol poisoning: unconsciousness, slowed breathing and choking on vomit
Dehydration and fluid loss from ADH suppression
REM sleep suppression and fragmentation
Behavioral disinhibition
Liver stress and gastric irritation
alcohol.visualizer_note: Deceptively harmful: dehydration, disinhibition and real overdose risk (alcohol poisoning, choking on vomit). Rated the most harmful drug overall in expert rankings.

nitrous.name: Nitrous Oxide (N₂O)

Inhaled.note: Counted in cream chargers (about 8 g each, roughly one balloon), not mg. In grams (PsychonautWiki): threshold about 4 g, light 4–8 g, common 8–16 g, strong 16–40 g, heavy 40 g and up. IMPORTANT: these tiers only describe how intense one sitting feels. They do not bound the nerve-damage risk, which tracks the TOTAL number of balloons per session and per week, not the size of any single hit. There is no known safe cumulative amount. People who develop nerve damage are usually heavy or regular users getting through many chargers, or using large catering tanks where it is very easy to lose count. The toxic dose is undefined.

nitrous.sleep_strategy: No real effect on sleep, since it clears within minutes. The only overnight concern is not lying down or being left alone while still unsteady, and not chaining balloons late into the night.

essential.short: Setting: Sit down before you inhale.
essential.detail: Nitrous causes an abrupt loss of balance and can make you faint. Sitting down, ideally on the floor and away from roads, water, edges and hard corners, means that if you pass out you slump rather than fall. Falls are a real risk, which is why harm reduction services tell you to sit down first.

essential.short: B12: A B12 supplement is sensible if you use regularly, but it is not a licence to use more.
essential.detail: Nitrous chemically inactivates vitamin B12. It oxidises the cobalt core and blocks the B12-dependent enzyme methionine synthase, which is what leads to nerve damage. Keeping B12 stores up is low-risk and reasonable, but there is no good evidence that supplements reliably prevent nerve damage in heavy users, because the deficiency is functional rather than dietary. The only dependable protection is limiting how much gas you get through. People eating little B12 (vegans and vegetarians) or with gut absorption problems are at higher risk.

sources.label: Neurologic & thrombotic complications of chronic nitrous abuse (PMC9859688)

bonus.short: Equipment: Use a balloon and a proper cracker or dispenser. Never inhale straight from a charger or tank.
bonus.detail: Gas leaving a charger or tank is under high pressure and extremely cold, and leaves the container at around -40 C, so it can cold-burn the nose, lips, mouth, throat and lungs. In rare case reports the swelling that followed blocked the airway and needed emergency hospital treatment. Releasing it into a balloon first lets it warm and drop in pressure to something safe to breathe. Cheap plastic dispensers have also burst under pressure.

bonus.short: Supply: Prefer small chargers over large catering tanks.
bonus.detail: Large cylinders and tanks make it very easy to lose track of how much you have inhaled and to take huge volumes quickly. That is the pattern most linked to oxygen starvation and to the cumulative dose that causes nerve damage. EUDA flags the shift to bigger tanks as a rising-harm trend in Europe.

sources.label: EUDA: Recreational use of nitrous oxide: a growing concern for Europe

during.focus: Keep oxygen in the loop and stay seated. The acute danger is suffocation; the long-term danger is total volume.

essential.short: ⚠️ Oxygen: Never use a mask or bag, or an enclosed space (car, tent), and don't breathe in and out of the balloon.
essential.detail: Pure nitrous contains no oxygen, unlike the 50/50 medical mix. Re-breathing it, sealing it over your face with a mask, putting a bag over your head, or filling a small closed space starves the brain of oxygen. If you pass out with a mask strapped on or a bag on your head, you suffocate. People have died this way. This is the one genuinely life-threatening rule.

essential.short: Pace: One balloon at a time, with normal breaths of fresh air in between.
essential.detail: Spacing balloons lets your blood oxygen recover between hits and keeps the total volume down. Chaining balloons back to back is what drives both the immediate oxygen-starvation risk and the cumulative B12 and nerve-damage risk. Because each hit lasts only a minute or two, the urge to redose straight away is strong, so decide a limit before you start.

essential.short: Position: Stay seated and still. Do not walk, dance, climb or stand near roads, water or edges while it hits.
essential.detail: Nitrous briefly wipes out gross and fine motor control, balance and coordination. Standing or moving during the peak is how people fall, and the peak arrives within seconds. Wait until you are fully steady before getting up.

essential.short: Mixing: Go easy if you've been drinking or using other depressants or dissociatives (alcohol, GHB/GBL, ketamine, opioids).
essential.detail: These add to the sedation and loss of coordination from nitrous and raise the chance of an unexpected blackout, and passing out brings a risk of choking on vomit if you are not on your side. TripSit rates nitrous with alcohol, GHB/GBL, opioids and tramadol as 'Caution' for exactly this reason, and ketamine and other dissociatives add incoordination on top. Not a deadly combination in itself, but a reason to slow right down, not chain balloons, and stay seated.

bonus.short: Limit: Cap the total balloons for the night and the week.
bonus.detail: The nerve-damage risk tracks how many balloons you get through over time, not how strong a single hit feels, and there is no known safe cumulative amount. Occasional small use carries far less risk than regular heavy sessions or daily use. Keeping session and weekly totals low is the single most effective step.

sources.label: EUDA: Recreational use of nitrous oxide: a growing concern for Europe
Neurologic & thrombotic complications of chronic nitrous abuse (PMC9859688)

bonus.short: Driving: Don't drive or cycle after using.
bonus.detail: Even though the effects are brief, coordination and judgement are impaired around use, and driving while impaired is dangerous and illegal.

essential.short: If someone passes out: lay them on their side and check their breathing. Call emergency services if they do not come round quickly.
essential.detail: Most people recover within minutes, but combined with alcohol or other depressants a person can lose consciousness and choke on vomit. The recovery position keeps the airway clear. Don't leave anyone who is drowsy or unresponsive on their back or unmonitored.

bonus.short: Watch for warning signs: tingling, numbness, pins-and-needles, weakness or unsteady walking in the days after.
bonus.detail: These are the early signs of B12-related nerve damage from nitrous. If they appear, that is a clear signal to stop and see a doctor. Early treatment gives the best chance of full recovery, while continued use can make the damage lasting.

sources.label: Neurologic & thrombotic complications of chronic nitrous abuse (PMC9859688)

essential.short: Body check: persistent numbness or tingling in hands/feet, weakness, or an unsteady, stumbling walk means see a doctor.
essential.detail: B12 deficiency caused by nitrous can lead to nerve damage in the hands and feet and, when severe, to degeneration of the spinal cord that can progress to difficulty walking and even lasting disability. Tell the doctor you have been using nitrous and ask specifically about B12. Treatment is B12 plus stopping the gas, and recovery is best when caught early.

sources.label: Neurologic & thrombotic complications of chronic nitrous abuse (PMC9859688)

bonus.short: Diet: if you use nitrous and eat little B12 (vegan/vegetarian) or have absorption problems, get a B12 check.
bonus.detail: Low baseline B12 leaves less buffer against nitrous inactivating it, so nerve symptoms can appear after less use. A blood test (B12, and ideally homocysteine and MMA) is worth having, but a normal result is not a green light to use heavily.

sources.label: Neurologic & thrombotic complications of chronic nitrous abuse (PMC9859688)

risks: Vitamin B12 inactivation leading to nerve damage (tingling, numbness, weakness, unsteady walking) and, when severe, spinal-cord degeneration that can be lasting. This is the main danger of heavy or regular use
Fainting and suffocation from lack of oxygen, especially with a mask or bag, in a car or enclosed space, or straight from a large tank
Falls and injury from sudden loss of balance while standing
Frostbite / cold burns to lips, mouth and airway from gas taken straight off a charger or tank
Strong pull to keep redosing ('chaining' balloons), which is what pushes the cumulative dose up
Blood-clot risk (DVT / pulmonary embolism) via raised homocysteine in heavy users
nitrous.visualizer_note: The real danger is cumulative and preventable. Short, moreish hits drive compulsive redosing, and heavy or regular use inactivates vitamin B12 and can cause lasting nerve and spinal-cord damage. There is also a real risk of fainting or suffocation whenever oxygen is cut off, by a mask, a bag, an enclosed space, or breathing straight from a large tank.

poppers.name: Poppers (Alkyl Nitrites)
poppers.sleep_strategy: Poppers do not disturb sleep on their own, because the effect is gone within a couple of minutes. Any wakefulness comes from the setting (sex, clubbing, other drugs), not the poppers.

essential.short: ⚠️ Erection drugs: never use poppers if you've taken Viagra (sildenafil), Cialis (tadalafil), Levitra (vardenafil) or any nitrate.
essential.detail: Both poppers and PDE5-inhibitor erection drugs widen blood vessels. Together they can cause a catastrophic and potentially fatal drop in blood pressure, leading to fainting, shock and death. A UK death review recorded a fatality from 'combined alkyl nitrate and tadalafil toxicity'. This is the single most important warning.

sources.label: Corkery et al. 2025: UK poppers deaths (PMC)

essential.short: ⚠️ Inhale only, never swallow: drinking poppers can be fatal.
essential.detail: Swallowing alkyl nitrites causes methaemoglobinaemia, in which the blood can no longer carry oxygen, leading to blue skin, coma and death. A UK review found at least 10 swallowing deaths, with methaemoglobin measured in only two of them, at 38% and 46%. Keep the bottle well away from drinks and out of reach of others.

sources.label: Corkery et al. 2025: UK poppers deaths (PMC)

essential.short: Health check: best avoided if you have heart problems, low or unstable blood pressure, anaemia or glaucoma, or are pregnant.
essential.detail: Poppers sharply drop blood pressure and can trigger an abnormal heart rhythm ('sudden sniffing death'). These conditions make that swing dangerous, and glaucoma and anaemia are specific contraindications across harm-reduction sources.

bonus.short: Blood-pressure medication: the same crash risk applies, so avoid poppers if you are on any nitrate or blood-pressure drug.
bonus.detail: Nitroglycerin and other nitrate/antihypertensive medicines are vasodilators too; stacking poppers on top can drop blood pressure dangerously, the same mechanism as the erection-drug interaction.

bonus.short: Your own bottle: use your own, keep it capped and upright.
bonus.detail: Spilled liquid burns skin and lips and irritates the eyes, and open or stale product loses potency and worsens headaches. A capped, upright, personal bottle avoids spills and cross-contamination.

during.focus: Stay seated or steady, waft the vapour rather than pressing the bottle to your nose, and keep flames well away.

essential.short: Sit or steady yourself: the head-rush is a sharp blood-pressure drop, so you can feel faint or fall.
essential.detail: Rapid widening of the blood vessels lowers blood pressure within seconds, causing light-headedness and fainting, especially the first time or when standing up. Sit or lean on something solid before you inhale.

essential.short: Waft, do not press: hold the bottle a little away and breathe the vapour, because the liquid burns skin, lips and eyes.
essential.detail: Alkyl nitrites are corrosive; direct contact causes chemical burns and rashes around the nose and mouth, and splashes irritate the eyes and throat. Wafting the vapour toward your nose avoids skin contact.

essential.short: Flame: never use near cigarettes, candles or lighters, because the vapour and liquid are extremely flammable.
essential.detail: Alkyl nitrites are highly flammable and can ignite from a nearby flame or ember. Keep all ignition sources well away while a bottle is open.

essential.short: Blue lips or breathlessness: stop, get away from the fumes, and get emergency help if it does not clear quickly.
essential.detail: Blue-grey lips or fingertips plus shortness of breath signal methaemoglobinaemia, meaning part of your haemoglobin has been changed into a form that cannot carry oxygen. It builds up with heavy or non-stop use. Stop and get away from the fumes, because mild cases usually settle once the exposure ends. Fresh air does not reverse the change in the blood, so if lips stay blue or breathing is hard, get emergency care. Severe cases are treated in hospital with an antidote.

sources.label: Corkery et al. 2025: UK poppers deaths (PMC)

bonus.short: Pace it: the effect fades within a minute and tempts a repeat, and frequent redosing brings headaches and more strain.
bonus.detail: The very short duration drives repeated sniffing; each redose stacks blood-pressure swings and commonly causes headaches. Take breaks rather than sniffing continuously.

bonus.short: Alcohol: mixing raises the risk of passing out or choking.
bonus.detail: Heavy alcohol adds to the blood-pressure drop and sedation, increasing the chance of fainting or choking; it also blunts your judgement about how much you're using.

bonus.short: Sex: poppers lower inhibitions, which can lead to riskier decisions such as skipping condoms.
bonus.detail: Disinhibition and heightened libido are part of the effect; harm-reduction sources link poppers use during sex to reduced condom use, STI transmission and injury. Decide on protection before you start.

essential.short: Vision: if colours look off, or you notice a central blur or a blind spot, stop using, because poppers can damage the retina.
essential.detail: 'Poppers maculopathy' is retinal photoreceptor damage linked especially to isopropyl nitrite (more common since isopropyl nitrite replaced isobutyl nitrite in Europe, after the 2006 EU reclassification). It often improves after stopping but can be lasting, so treat any vision change as a signal to stop.

bonus.short: Headache: a headache afterwards is common and usually settles with rest and water; it's worse with stale product.
bonus.detail: Widening of the blood vessels in the brain, plus repeated dosing, causes the classic poppers headache. Older, degraded liquid makes it worse, which is another reason to keep bottles fresh and capped.

essential.short: Vision persisting: if any vision change hasn't cleared by the next day, stop entirely and see an optician or doctor.
essential.detail: Both temporary and permanent vision loss have been reported after poppers use. Persistent changes need an eye exam, and continuing to use risks making retinal damage permanent.

bonus.short: Skin: crusty patches or a rash around the nose or lips come from liquid contact. Let them heal and waft the vapour next time.
bonus.detail: Repeated skin contact with the corrosive liquid causes crusty lesions and rashes around the nose and mouth. They heal once contact stops; wafting instead of pressing the bottle prevents them.

risks: Potentially fatal with erection drugs (Viagra, Cialis, Levitra) or any nitrate or blood-pressure medication, because blood pressure can crash catastrophically
Swallowing is potentially fatal, because it causes methaemoglobinaemia (the blood can no longer carry oxygen)
Sudden blood-pressure drop causes dizziness, fainting and falls; rare 'sudden sniffing death' from a heart-rhythm disturbance
Isopropyl nitrite can damage the retina ('poppers maculopathy'), causing vision changes that are sometimes permanent
Corrosive to skin, lips and eyes, and highly flammable, so keep it away from flames
Risky with heart or blood-pressure conditions, anaemia, glaucoma, and in pregnancy
poppers.visualizer_note: Inhaled poppers rarely kill on their own. The real dangers are combining them with erection drugs or blood-pressure medication, which can crash your blood pressure fatally, swallowing them, which can cause fatal methaemoglobinaemia, fainting from the sudden pressure drop, and, with isopropyl nitrite, lasting damage to the retina.

cannabis.name: Cannabis
cannabis.sleep_strategy: May help sleep onset, but reduces REM quality.

essential.short: Safety: Check your source and avoid synthetic cannabinoids.
essential.detail: The illicit cannabis market carries significant risk of adulteration with synthetic cannabinoids sprayed onto CBD flower. Synthetics are full CB1 agonists with unpredictable dose-response curves, frequently leading to severe intoxication, psychosis, and cardiovascular emergencies.

essential.short: Edibles: Wait at least two hours before taking any more.
essential.detail: An edible can take 30 to 90 minutes to come on, and sometimes longer on a full stomach. Most bad edible experiences come from taking a second dose before the first one arrives, then getting both at once. Start with one low dose and wait it out.

essential.short: Environment: Choose a comfortable, familiar setting.
essential.detail: Cannabis amplifies environmental stimuli. A safe, familiar setting with trusted people significantly reduces the probability of anxiety or paranoia episodes.

essential.short: Faintness: Sit or lie down if dizzy, and stand up slowly.
essential.detail: Cannabis widens blood vessels in the body and raises heart rate. Combined with standing and sweating, this creates a risk of a sudden blood-pressure drop when you stand up, causing dizziness or fainting. If you feel light-headed, sit or lie down and get up slowly. A snack or juice helps general energy but does not itself fix the blood-pressure drop.

essential.short: Caution: Avoid mixing with tobacco or alcohol.
essential.detail: THC itself does not depress breathing at recreational doses, which is why there is no fatal overdose from plain cannabis. Sprayed synthetic cannabinoids are a different matter and have caused acute breathing problems. With plain cannabis, tobacco mainly adds dependence, tar and carbon monoxide, plus nausea and dizziness. Alcohol is the riskier mix: drinking before cannabis raises peak blood THC, and alcohol widens blood vessels too, so nausea, dizziness and vomiting are common.

bonus.short: Hydration: Sip water regularly to manage dry mouth.
bonus.detail: Cannabis reduces saliva production via CB1 receptors in the salivary glands. Steady water sipping alleviates discomfort and maintains baseline hydration.

essential.short: Appetite stimulation: Keep any late-night snack small.
essential.detail: Cannabis stimulates hypothalamic appetite pathways. However, a very large late meal is linked to more night waking and a slower drop into sleep, so keep the snack modest.

bonus.short: Food: A light protein and carbohydrate snack is sufficient.
bonus.detail: A small portion of slow-digesting protein and complex carbohydrates satisfies appetite while supporting overnight recovery without disrupting sleep.

bonus.short: Relaxation: Gentle stretching may help relieve mild tension.
bonus.detail: Cannabis relaxes muscles rather than tensing them. Gentle stretching still eases tension you brought with you and helps settle the body for sleep.

essential.short: Residual effects: Cannabis aftereffects are common. Hydrate and move.
essential.detail: Residual cannabinoids can produce morning fogginess and lethargy. Water and movement help you feel more alert, but neither speeds up how fast THC leaves the body: it is stored in fat and cleared over days.

bonus.short: Cognition: Expect some reduced processing speed.
bonus.detail: THC suppresses REM sleep, which is critical for memory consolidation. Reduced cognitive processing is normal; plan for a lighter workload.

risks: Orthostatic hypotension (faintness/dizziness)
Anxiety or paranoia episodes
Edible overdose from redosing before the effects arrive
Adulteration with synthetic cannabinoids
cannabis.visualizer_note: Low physiological harm with no fatal overdose from THC; main issues are a sharp rise in heart rate with a drop in blood pressure, faintness, anxiety and synthetic-cannabinoid adulteration.

dmt.name: DMT

Vaporized.note: These tiers are for VAPORIZED or smoked freebase DMT. Swallowed DMT does nothing on its own, because gut enzymes (monoamine oxidase) destroy it, so oral use only works combined with an MAOI (ayahuasca or pharmahuasca; changa is smoked, not swallowed). That is a completely different experience: much longer, roughly 2–10 h depending on the preparation, dependent on the MAOI, and with a far riskier interaction profile (see risks and combinations). Vaporized strength varies a lot with purity and technique, and a full 'breakthrough' is often 40 mg or more, though poor vaporizing wastes material. Figures follow PsychonautWiki. TripSit lists somewhat lower tiers (common about 15–25 mg), which reflects real-world variance, so start low.

dmt.sleep_strategy: Effects are over within ~15–30 minutes and after-effects fade within the hour, so normal sleep is usually possible the same night. Allow quiet time to reintegrate before bed.

essential.short: Set & setting: Calm, familiar space with a sober person present.
essential.detail: DMT is one of the most intense psychedelics but also one of the shortest. The psychological outcome depends heavily on mindset ('set') and surroundings ('setting'); people with a personal or family history of psychosis or mood disorders face a higher risk of a distressing reaction. A trusted, sober companion makes an overwhelming experience manageable.

essential.short: Position: Sit back or lie down before you inhale, because you will lose motor control.
essential.detail: At common and strong doses, voluntary movement and spatial awareness disappear within seconds and stay gone through the ~2–8 minute peak. Being already seated or reclined on the floor (away from edges, water, heat sources and crowds) prevents falls and injury while you are physically helpless.

essential.short: ⚠️ MAOI route is different: oral/ayahuasca use, or use while on an MAOI, is a higher-risk scenario.
essential.detail: Smoked DMT alone is low in toxicity, but the moment an MAOI is involved, whether ayahuasca, pharmahuasca, changa or an MAOI antidepressant, the risk profile changes sharply. MAOIs block the breakdown of serotonin and tyramine, so combining them with SSRIs, SNRIs, other serotonergic drugs, stimulants (cocaine, amphetamine, MDMA) or tyramine-rich foods can cause serotonin syndrome or a dangerous blood-pressure surge with a stroke risk. If you take any serotonergic medication, do not add an MAOI-based DMT preparation.

essential.short: ⚠️ Lithium and tramadol: Do not combine, because both sharply raise seizure risk.
essential.detail: In 62 online reports of a classic psychedelic taken with lithium, 47% involved seizures and 39% involved medical attention. TripSit rates this pairing Dangerous. Tramadol independently lowers the seizure threshold (TripSit: Unsafe). Combining either with DMT risks a seizure.

sources.label: Nayak et al. 2021: Psychedelics + Lithium and Seizures

bonus.short: Dose: Know your source and start with a light dose to gauge potency.
bonus.detail: Freebase DMT strength and vaporizing efficiency vary widely, so the same 'hit' can be light for one person and a full breakthrough for another. Starting at a light dose (10–20 mg) lets you feel the onset before committing to a breakthrough, which can otherwise be overwhelming if unexpected.

during.focus: A sober sitter and a safe seated or lying position. The peak is total but brief.

essential.short: Sitter: Have someone sober stay with you until you can move and speak again.
essential.detail: At a full dose you are non-functional for the few minutes of the peak. A sitter keeps you physically safe, stops you wandering, and offers calm reassurance if the experience turns frightening. PsychonautWiki explicitly recommends a trip sitter for this substance.

essential.short: Stay put: Don't stand, walk, or move to music until effects fully subside.
essential.detail: Motor coordination and awareness of your real surroundings are gone at the peak, so a festival environment full of crowds, edges, water and traffic is genuinely hazardous. Stay seated or lying down for the whole experience.

essential.short: If it is overwhelming: it is brief, so breathe, stay reclined and let it pass.
essential.detail: DMT is among the most intense psychedelics but also the shortest-acting: the peak resolves within a few minutes and the whole experience within roughly 15–30 minutes. Knowing it will end quickly is itself a grounding tool during a difficult passage.

bonus.short: Avoid stacking with cannabis or stimulants in the moment.
bonus.detail: Cannabis has an unexpectedly strong and unpredictable synergy with psychedelics; stimulants (cocaine, amphetamine) add anxiety, thought loops and cardiovascular strain on top of DMT's own heart-rate/blood-pressure spike. TripSit rates both pairings Caution.

essential.short: Cardio recovery: Rest and sit up slowly. The spike in heart rate and blood pressure is brief but real.
essential.detail: In controlled dosing studies, DMT produced dose-dependent rises in blood pressure, heart rate, pupil diameter and body temperature, peaking within about two minutes and largely gone by 30 minutes. The surge is transient, but if you have a heart condition or uncontrolled hypertension this brief cardiovascular strain is the main physical caution.

essential.short: Reintegration: Take quiet time to reorient before moving on.
essential.detail: Even though it is short, a breakthrough can be deeply disorienting. A few calm minutes to reorient, sitting still with water and a familiar voice, reduces leftover anxiety before you rejoin the event.

bonus.short: Redosing: Effects fade fast and tolerance barely builds, but each dose repeats the hit to your heart.
bonus.detail: DMT shows little acute tolerance, so redosing 'works' in a way it would not for most psychedelics. Blood pressure still rises with each dose, though the heart-rate jump shrinks on quick repeats, so space doses out and do not chase the experience back to back.

essential.short: Expect a clear head: unlike long psychedelics, there is usually little hangover.
essential.detail: Smoked DMT clears the body within about half an hour and after-effects fade within the hour, so next-day physical residue is usually minimal. The main exception is if the experience itself was psychologically difficult.

bonus.short: Check in: If the experience was distressing, talk it through with someone you trust.
bonus.detail: Intense breakthroughs can surface difficult psychological material. People with a personal or family history of psychosis or mood disorders are at higher risk of lingering upset; persistent distress is worth discussing with a supportive person or professional.

risks: Overwhelming or frightening breakthrough; can trigger psychosis in those predisposed
Total loss of motor control at peak (fall / injury risk)
Sharp transient rise in heart rate & blood pressure
Serotonin syndrome or blood-pressure crisis: an MAOI (ayahuasca) plus SSRIs, stimulants or tyramine-rich foods
Seizure risk with lithium or tramadol
dmt.visualizer_note: On its own, vaporized DMT is physically low-risk and non-addictive. The real dangers are a frightening breakthrough with total loss of motor control, which needs a sitter and a safe seated or lying position, and a sharp but brief spike in heart rate and blood pressure. An MAOI (ayahuasca, pharmahuasca or MAOI medication) changes this entirely, adding serotonin syndrome and dangerous blood-pressure surges.

ketamine.name: Ketamine

Oral.note: Low oral bioavailability (~17–20%). Much higher doses needed.

ketamine.sleep_strategy: Wait for full offset. Do not mix with depressants.

essential.short: Stomach: Best to avoid eating in the ~90 minutes before, since ketamine can cause nausea and vomiting.
essential.detail: Ketamine frequently causes nausea and vomiting. At dissociative doses you cannot move, sit up or clear your own airway, so vomit can block it, and inhaled vomit can kill. Being on your side is what protects you, so do not take a heavy dose alone: have a sober person there who can turn you.

essential.short: Safety: Test your substance.
essential.detail: Samples sold as ketamine are usually ketamine, but close analogues such as 2-FDCK or DCK do turn up, and they last longer and are active at different doses. Standard reagents cannot tell these apart from ketamine, so use a Morris reagent kit or a lab drug-checking service.

bonus.short: Preparation: Crush to fine powder to protect nasal tissue.
bonus.detail: Large crystals dissolve slowly and scratch the nasal lining. Repeated snorting of coarse powder causes irritation and nosebleeds, so crush it fine first.

essential.short: Hydration: Drink to thirst. There is no need to force fluids.
essential.detail: Drink to thirst rather than forcing fluids. Long-term ketamine use damages the bladder lining (ketamine-induced cystitis), so bladder health matters, but unlike MDMA a single ketamine session carries no special water-intoxication risk. Just drink normally, neither forcing nor heavily restricting fluids.

essential.short: Movement: Pain signals are blocked, so take extreme care.
essential.detail: Ketamine blocks pain perception. Moving vigorously while anaesthetised is dangerous, because you cannot feel joint strain, muscle tears or ligament damage until the drug wears off.

essential.short: Balance: Sit down immediately if you feel unsteady.
essential.detail: Ketamine causes severe ataxia (loss of motor control) and spatial disorientation. Falling over is a common way people get hurt. If balance feels impaired, sit in a safe environment immediately.

essential.short: Environment: Low sensory input (dark, quiet space).
essential.detail: Coming down from ketamine leaves the user deeply disoriented and vulnerable. A calm, sensory-reduced environment aids psychological reintegration and prevents anxiety.

essential.short: Safety: Use the lateral recovery position if resting.
essential.detail: If a user is unresponsive or deeply sedated, the recovery position ensures airway patency. Monitor breathing and never leave an unconscious person on their back.

bonus.short: Supplements: Delay magnesium until the next day.
bonus.detail: Magnesium is used against MDMA jaw clenching, which ketamine does not cause. Ketamine also raises muscle tone rather than relaxing it, so magnesium does nothing useful on the night. Leave it for the next day if you want it.

essential.short: Body: Check for bruises or injuries.
essential.detail: Due to ketamine's anesthetic properties, injuries sustained during use may go unnoticed. A thorough physical check the next morning can reveal strains, bruises, or injuries that need attention.

bonus.short: Rest: Allow a full recovery day. Avoid redosing.
bonus.detail: Residual dissociation, cognitive impairment, and disorientation are common the day after. Ketamine's effects on memory consolidation and spatial perception can persist well past the active window.

risks: Bladder damage (ketamine cystitis)
Aspiration from vomiting while dissociated
Slowed or stopped breathing, deep sedation and choking on vomit if mixed with alcohol, GHB/GBL, benzos or opioids
Physical injury due to anaesthesia
Loss of motor control
ketamine.visualizer_note: Moderate. Bladder damage builds with repeated use, and you can injure yourself or choke on vomit while dissociated. Overdose risk climbs steeply if mixed with depressants.

lsd.name: LSD
lsd.sleep_strategy: Plan for complete insomnia during effects. Do not fight it.

essential.short: Test: Ehrlich reagent kit (rule out NBOMe). Additionally, DOx compounds (effects lasting up to 48 hours) are also substituted as LSD.
essential.detail: The illicit market sometimes substitutes LSD with 25I-NBOMe or DOx compounds, which can cause fatal heart events, seizures and severe narrowing of blood vessels at doses under a milligram. An Ehrlich reagent test turns purple for indoles, the family LSD belongs to. NBOMe and DOx are not indoles and give no colour change, so no reaction is a sure sign it is not LSD. A purple result rules those substitutes out but does not confirm the dose. The Loop found 25x-NBOMe sold as LSD at Boomtown 2018 with no LSD in it. NBOMe and DOx are the main blotter adulterants, and DOx effects can last 48 hours.

essential.short: Set & Setting: Trusted company, safe location.
essential.detail: LSD profoundly alters sensory perception and cognition for 8–12 hours. The psychological outcome is heavily dependent on the user's mindset ('set') and physical environment ('setting').

bonus.short: Nutrition: Eat a light, healthy meal beforehand.
bonus.detail: LSD can blunt appetite, though less strongly than stimulants do, for the whole trip. Eating a balanced meal before ensures the body has adequate fuel for 12+ hours of wakefulness.

essential.short: Nutrition: Have fruit or smoothies regularly, because hunger signals are suppressed.
essential.detail: LSD blunts appetite, less strongly than stimulants do, and it is easy to simply forget to eat. Going 10 to 12 hours without food leaves you shaky and drained.

essential.short: Hydration: Set reminders to drink.
essential.detail: Sensory overload and cognitive distortion make it easy to forget basic needs. External reminders from friends or phone alarms ensure consistent hydration.

bonus.short: Mindset: Change music or lighting if anxious.
bonus.detail: Anxiety during a psychedelic experience often comes from your surroundings. A simple change of scene, such as different music, moving outdoors, or adjusting the lighting, can shift things quickly.

essential.short: Mindset: Accept wakefulness. Do not try to force sleep.
essential.detail: Residual stimulation and difficulty sleeping are common for hours after the trip fades. Forcing sleep just builds frustration, so rest without expecting to sleep.

essential.short: Food: Protein + carbohydrates to restore caloric deficit.
essential.detail: After a long stretch of eating little, a meal with protein and carbohydrates helps you feel steady again. A protein and carbohydrate meal provides essential amino acids for recovery.

bonus.short: Activity: Gentle stretching and calming music.
bonus.detail: Physical tension from sympathetic arousal builds over the 12-hour duration. Gentle stretching releases this tension while calming music aids the transition.

essential.short: Rest: Plan for a full recovery day.
essential.detail: A 12-hour psychedelic experience combined with sleep deprivation results in profound fatigue. Plan for a recovery day with minimal obligations.

bonus.short: Afterglow: Expect residual visual effects and altered cognition for up to 24 hours.
bonus.detail: Mild residual visuals, tiredness and mood swings are common the next day. Lasting HPPD is a different condition, where perceptual changes carry on into daily life. Estimates of how common it is vary widely.

risks: Psychological crisis (challenging trip)
Accidents from impaired judgement
Peripheral vasoconstriction
Insomnia for 10 to 18 hours
lsd.visualizer_note: Physically very safe, with near-zero overdose risk. The danger is psychological, plus long insomnia during effects. Accidents and NBOMe sold as acid are the real lethal risks.

mushrooms.name: Mushrooms (Psilocybin)

Oral.note: Values are for dried Psilocybe cubensis. Other species vary a lot in strength, so a dose that suits one species can be far too much of another. Work out a fresh starting dose for anything new.

mushrooms.sleep_strategy: Insomnia likely until effects subside. Rest in darkness.

essential.short: Set & Setting: Critical for preventing challenging trips.
essential.detail: Psilocybin amplifies emotions and environmental stimuli. Ensure a positive mindset and a safe, comfortable environment. Have a trusted trip-sitter present if possible. Best avoided if you or a close relative has had psychosis or bipolar disorder.

essential.short: Dose: Start low (0.5–1 g dried) to gauge potency.
essential.detail: Potency varies significantly between species and batches. A standard dose is 1.5–2.5 g. Doses above 5 g strongly increase the risk of a psychological crisis and are best avoided in a recreational setting.

bonus.short: Stomach: Light meal or fasting to reduce nausea.
bonus.detail: Nausea on the come-up is thought to come mainly from psilocin acting on serotonin receptors in the gut, with the tough fungal fibre a possible second factor. An empty or light stomach reduces the volume that can come back up. Ginger is a well-established anti-nausea remedy, and a tea or lemon-tek is often gentler than eating whole mushrooms.

essential.short: Nausea: Breathe through the onset (20–60 minutes).
essential.detail: Nausea is common during the come-up phase. It typically passes once peak effects are established. Find a comfortable position and breathe deeply.

essential.short: Mindset: Do not resist the experience.
essential.detail: Anxiety often arises from resisting the dissolution of ego or control. Surrendering to the flow of the experience, even if challenging, is the safest psychological strategy.

bonus.short: Hydration: Keep water nearby and sip occasionally.
bonus.detail: While not a diuretic, psilocybin can make you forget to drink. Gentle reminders help maintain baseline hydration.

essential.short: Environment: Low stimulation. Allow the experience to settle.
essential.detail: The afterglow involves continued serotonin activity and reduced mental filtering. A quiet setting with few demands, such as walking outside, calm music and light food, lets your body and mind return to baseline without extra stress.

bonus.short: Food: Fresh fruit and healthy snacks.
bonus.detail: Appetite often returns as effects fade. Fresh, unprocessed foods often feel most palatable and nourishing.

essential.short: Mood: Usually an elevated afterglow.
essential.detail: Psilocybin often leaves a lasting positive mood lift. Use this window to reinforce healthy habits.

bonus.short: Rest: Allow for a relaxed schedule.
bonus.detail: A headache is common in the hours after the effects fade. Trials rate it mild to moderate, more often moderate after a larger dose, and it clears within about a day. The mind may be tired, but there is no physical hangover of the alcohol kind.

risks: Psychological distress (challenging trip); can trigger psychosis in vulnerable people
Nausea and vomiting
Fatal poisoning from misidentified wild mushrooms
Confusion and disorientation
mushrooms.visualizer_note: Among the lowest-harm substances. There is no fatal overdose from psilocybin itself, and the main risks are difficult trips and misidentified wild mushrooms.

cocaine.name: Cocaine
cocaine.sleep_strategy: Stop use 3–4 hours before bed. Sleep is very difficult.

essential.short: Test: Use a reagent kit; fentanyl strips are a sensible extra precaution.
essential.detail: In Europe, fentanyl contamination of cocaine is uncommon, unlike parts of North America, but it has caused deaths, so fentanyl test strips are a cheap precaution rather than a guarantee. A reagent kit (Morris, then Marquis, then Liebermann) can flag that something is wrong, but it cannot confirm the powder is cocaine, cannot measure purity, and will not reliably catch cuts such as levamisole or lidocaine. For that you need a lab drug-checking service.

sources.label: DanceSafe: How to use reagent kits

essential.short: ⚠️ Levamisole: The most dangerous of the common cocaine cuts.
essential.detail: Some street cocaine is cut with levamisole, a veterinary deworming agent. European drug checking finds it in roughly 3 to 8 percent of samples, far below US rates, but a single exposure can still do real damage. It can wipe out white blood cells (agranulocytosis) and cause skin necrosis and vasculitis. See a doctor about unexplained sores, mouth ulcers, fever or repeated infections after using.

essential.short: Hygiene: Use your own straw. Never share (Hepatitis C risk).
essential.detail: Micro-abrasions in the nasal cavity can transmit blood-borne pathogens like Hepatitis C. Sharing straws or bills is a plausible route, and hepatitis C has been found on used sniffing tools. Use a personal, clean tool.

bonus.short: Nasal care: Pre-moisturize with saline spray.
bonus.detail: Dry nasal membranes rupture easily. Pre-moistening with saline spray reduces damage and aids absorption.

essential.short: ⚠️ Alcohol danger: Cocaethylene formation is lethal.
essential.detail: Combining cocaine + alcohol forms cocaethylene in the liver. This metabolite is significantly more cardiotoxic than cocaine alone, and post-mortem and emergency-department data link its presence to a much higher chance of sudden death.

essential.short: ⚠️ Chest pain: Stop and get emergency help. Do not try to wait it out.
essential.detail: Cocaine narrows blood vessels while pushing up heart rate, forcing the heart to pump against high pressure. The risk of a heart attack rises roughly 24 times in the hour after a dose, and chest pain is the most common reason cocaine users end up in an emergency department. Chest tightness or pain needs medical assessment, not just stopping.

sources.label: Mittleman et al. 1999, Circulation: cocaine and myocardial infarction onset
American Heart Association: cocaine and cardiovascular risk

bonus.short: Preparation: Fine powder absorbs better and reduces tissue damage.
bonus.detail: Large crystals damage tissue and are poorly absorbed. Rinsing with saline between sessions helps limit tissue damage.

essential.short: Comedown: Expect anxiety and cravings.
essential.detail: Cocaine has a sharp, unpleasant crash. Recognize the craving as a chemical signal, not a true need. Do not redose to delay the inevitable.

bonus.short: Nasal care: Thorough saline rinse.
bonus.detail: Rinsing the nose clears leftover powder and keeps the lining moist. Septum damage comes mainly from repeated narrowing of the blood vessels starving the tissue of blood, so a rinse helps but does not undo that.

essential.short: Recovery: Rest and hydration.
essential.detail: The crash is a rebound in the brain's reward system, and the exact mechanism is still debated. Expect low mood and irritability. Sleep and time are the primary recovery mechanisms.

bonus.short: Nasal check: Inspect for bleeding or scabs.
bonus.detail: Use a water-based saline gel rather than an oil. Oils repeatedly inhaled into the nose can settle in the lungs and cause lipoid pneumonia. Bleeding or crusting that keeps coming back needs a doctor.

risks: Severe cardiotoxicity (heart attack)
Cocaethylene formation (with alcohol)
Adulteration (levamisole, phenacetin, lidocaine, caffeine; rarely fentanyl in Europe)
Compulsive redosing
cocaine.visualizer_note: High cardiotoxicity and strong compulsion; overdose risk is real and rises sharply with binge use or alcohol (cocaethylene).

amphetamine.name: Amphetamine

Oral.note: Street speed varies a lot in purity, so use a drug-checking service. SaferParty advises a ceiling of about 50 mg per 12 hours. Wet amphetamine paste must be fully dried before dosing, because leftover solvents are toxic.

amphetamine.sleep_strategy: Sleep is very difficult until the drug clears. Do not redose to delay it; plan recovery time.

essential.short: Meal: Eat a large, nutritious meal beforehand, because your appetite will be fully suppressed.
essential.detail: Amphetamines strongly suppress appetite and cause dry mouth, so eating during the session is hard. A meal of complex carbohydrates and protein beforehand is the easiest way to bank energy for hours of stimulated activity.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): some people pre-load magnesium for vasoconstriction and muscle tension.
bonus.detail: Amphetamines cause vasoconstriction and muscle tension. Magnesium is often taken for this, but no good human study shows an oral supplement blunts it.

during.focus: Cardiac safety and core temperature management.

essential.short: Rest and fluids: break roughly hourly to cool down, and sip about half a litre an hour.
essential.detail: Amphetamines put intense, continuous strain on the heart and blood vessels, raising heart rate, blood pressure and body temperature, while the dopamine flood masks pain and tiredness. Regular breaks out of the heat let all three settle, and about half a litre of water or an isotonic drink an hour covers what you sweat out without overdoing it.

essential.short: Pain and fatigue are masked, so pace yourself and try not to push through strain or injury.
essential.detail: Dopamine and noradrenaline release blunts pain and fatigue signals. The warnings get much quieter, so people push into joint damage, muscle tears or overheating before they notice.

essential.short: ⚠️ Never combine with MAOIs or tricyclic antidepressants. Other antidepressants: ask a doctor first.
essential.detail: Amphetamine with an MAOI, including moclobemide or the herb Syrian rue, can cause a dangerous blood-pressure surge, which can be fatal. Drugchecking Berlin puts tricyclic antidepressants in the same life-threatening group. Do not use amphetamine at all with either. SSRIs and SNRIs are a much smaller concern: TripSit's combination chart rates that pairing low risk, and doctors often prescribe the two together, so ask your doctor rather than assume it is unsafe.

bonus.short: Nutrition: Consume liquid calories (shakes, gels) despite zero appetite.
bonus.detail: Solid food is unpalatable on amphetamines. Protein shakes, carbohydrate gels, or smoothies provide circulating glucose and prevent muscle catabolism.

essential.short: Food: Try to eat despite low appetite.
essential.detail: Despite zero appetite, the body is in severe caloric deficit after hours of stimulated activity without food. Even small portions of protein and carbohydrates prevent continued muscle catabolism.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): vitamin C for general recovery, not to 'flush out' the drug.
bonus.detail: Gram-level vitamin C does not meaningfully acidify urine. Studies find even 4 g a day barely shifts it. So it does not speed up amphetamine clearance or shorten the comedown, despite the common claim. It is still useful for general antioxidant and nutrient replacement after a depleting night.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): magnesium for muscle tightness.
bonus.detail: Jaw clenching and muscle tension come from the drug acting on the nervous system, not from narrowed blood vessels. Magnesium helps some people and replaces what a heavy night depletes, but the trial evidence for cramps is weak.

essential.short: Mood: Expect lethargy and low mood (dopamine depletion).
essential.detail: Amphetamines deplete dopamine stores, resulting in intense lethargy, inability to feel pleasure (anhedonia), and emotional instability. This is a temporary neurochemical deficit.

bonus.short: Recovery (optional): some people take L-Tyrosine the next day (a dopamine precursor; evidence is limited).
bonus.detail: Tyrosine is what dopamine is built from, but the enzyme that converts it is already saturated at normal dietary levels, so extra tyrosine has not been shown to speed recovery.

risks: Severe cardiovascular strain (blood pressure/heart rate)
Hyperthermia (masked overheating)
Exhaustion and physical injury
Stimulant psychosis (with sleep deprivation)
amphetamine.visualizer_note: Sustained cardiovascular strain, hyperthermia and heavy sleep loss; overdose is less abrupt than opioids but real at high doses.

mdma.name: MDMA

Oral.note: Max: 1.5 mg/kg (men), 1.3 mg/kg (women). Effects plateau at ~125–150 mg; higher doses increase toxicity, not euphoria.

Insufflated.note: Dose at approximately half the oral amount. Described as very unpleasant and causes nasal tissue irritation. Not recommended.

mdma.sleep_strategy: Expect little or broken sleep the first night. It gets easier once the effects fully fade.

essential.short: Dose: Around 1.5 mg/kg is a common guideline, and staying under about 150 mg keeps toxicity lower. Higher doses add side-effects, not much extra euphoria.
essential.detail: The neurobehavioral effect plateaus around 125–150 mg. Exceeding this does not increase empathy or euphoria, but does increase amphetamine-like stimulation, jaw clenching (bruxism), and neurotoxicity.

essential.short: ⚠️ CRITICAL: Pill identity & content are extremely unreliable. Samples sold as 'MDMA' may be caffeine, other stimulants, or contain no MDMA at all (at one 2021 UK festival, ~30% of 'MDMA' samples were caffeine). High-dose pills (250–300+ mg) circulate widely. Always test before consuming.
essential.detail: Identical-looking pills can contain completely different drugs. One batch might be genuine MDMA, and the next batch with the same logo might be caffeine, a synthetic cathinone (4-CMC), an NBOMe compound, PMA/PMMA, or even a nitazene opioid, which have been linked to deaths. Many modern pills also exceed 200 mg, well above the 1.3 to 1.5 mg per kg body-weight ceiling. Appearance and branding are NOT reliable, so test with a reagent kit or a drug-checking service.

bonus.short: Supplements: ALA and ALCAR are sometimes taken as antioxidants, but the evidence is weak.
bonus.detail: The idea is that antioxidants such as Alpha-Lipoic Acid (ALA) and Acetyl-L-Carnitine (ALCAR) buffer the oxidative stress from MDMA. This protection has only been shown in animal studies and is unproven in humans. It does not replace the measures that actually reduce harm: limiting your dose, staying cool, and spacing use 4–6 weeks apart.

during.focus: Regulating core temperature and water intake.

essential.short: Hydration: 300 to 500 ml an hour, at the higher end if dancing. Make it an electrolyte drink or eat something salty, not plain water alone.
essential.detail: MDMA raises antidiuretic hormone (ADH), so the kidneys hold on to water and urinating becomes difficult. Drinking past that point dilutes your blood sodium and causes hyponatremia, which has killed people at events. Most reported cases, and the reported deaths, have been in women, so the limit matters even more for them. Electrolyte drinks or salty snacks are better than plain water alone, but the amount matters more than what is in it.

essential.short: Heat: Take regular cooling breaks and step out of the heat whenever you feel too warm.
essential.detail: MDMA impairs the body's thermoregulatory center. When combined with crowded spaces and dancing, core body temperatures can reach dangerous levels (hyperthermia), which simultaneously multiplies neurotoxicity.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): some people take vitamin C and magnesium during the roll.
bonus.detail: Vitamin C is taken as an antioxidant and magnesium for jaw clenching. Neither has been tested in people for this, so treat both as optional.

essential.short: Do not take 5-HTP within 24 hours of MDMA.
essential.detail: Taking 5-HTP while MDMA is still active can push serotonin too high and bring on mild to moderate serotonin syndrome. DanceSafe advises waiting at least 8 hours; we advise 24 hours to be safe. The brain needs up to 4 weeks to rebuild normal serotonin levels.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): magnesium to ease jaw tension.
bonus.detail: Some people take magnesium at the end of the night for jaw and muscle tension. This has not been tested in people for MDMA, so treat it as optional.

essential.short: Mood: Be ready for a mood dip, which usually peaks 2–3 days after use (the 'Tuesday Dip').
essential.detail: Significant serotonin depletion occurs. The lowest mood point rarely hits the next day, but rather 48–72 hours later. Recognize this as a temporary neurochemical deficit, not a permanent psychological state. This is characterized by sadness, irritability, and insomnia.

bonus.short: Recovery (optional): some people take 5-HTP with green tea extract (EGCG) after 24 h to support serotonin recovery.
bonus.detail: The idea is that EGCG slows the breakdown of 5-HTP in the gut so more of it reaches the brain. This is untested in people, and at best it eases the low mood rather than speeding recovery. Wait a full 24 hours after your last dose either way.

bonus.short: Nutrition: Eat regular meals, even if your appetite is low.
bonus.detail: Regular meals help you recover, but food alone does not raise brain serotonin much: the tryptophan in a high-protein meal competes with the other amino acids in it for the same route into the brain.

risks: Hyponatremia (water intoxication from ADH release)
Hyperthermia (overheating)
Serotonin syndrome with MAOIs (SSRIs mostly blunt the effect, but redosing to push through that blunting is where it gets dangerous)
Severe serotonin depletion (neurochemical crash)
mdma.visualizer_note: Neurotoxic and dehydrating; the main killers are hyperthermia and water intoxication (hyponatremia), not a simple 'overdose'.

caffeine.name: Caffeine

Oral.note: One cup of coffee is roughly 90 to 200 mg. EFSA: for healthy adults, no safety concern up to 200 mg in one dose, or 400 mg across a day. In pregnancy the figure is 200 mg a day.

caffeine.sleep_strategy: Avoid caffeine less than 6 hours before planned sleep.

essential.short: Timing: Stop intake 6–8 hours before planned sleep.
essential.detail: Caffeine has a half-life of about 5 hours in healthy adults, ranging from 2 to 12 depending on the person. Taking 200 mg late leaves plenty still active at bedtime, which cuts deep slow-wave sleep and the tissue repair it supports.

bonus.short: Hydration: Drink water in the heat.
bonus.detail: Drinking water alongside caffeine is still wise in the heat, though caffeine itself does not worsen the fluid loss from exercise.

essential.short: Limit: 200 mg at once, up to 400 mg across the day.
essential.detail: For healthy adults, EFSA sees no safety concern up to 200 mg in a single dose, or 400 mg spread across a day, and the US FDA cites the same 400 mg daily figure. EFSA sets 200 mg a day in pregnancy. Above that, anxiety, tremor and stomach upset get more likely. Tolerance varies a lot between people.

sources.label: US FDA: Spilling the Beans on Caffeine

essential.short: Avoid mixing with other stimulants (added cardiac strain).
essential.detail: Caffeine alongside MDMA, amphetamines or cocaine adds load to the heart, raising heart rate and blood pressure, and can worsen anxiety and physical discomfort. The extra caffeine is generally unnecessary next to a stimulant and offers little benefit. TripSit classifies these pairings as 'Caution' rather than dangerous.

bonus.short: Hydration: Water with every caffeinated drink.
bonus.detail: Caffeine's diuretic effect is mild, and studies show exercise cancels it out, so sweat is the real fluid loss. Drink for the dancing, not for the coffee.

essential.short: Sleep: If taken late, accept reduced sleep quality.
essential.detail: Caffeine blocks the receptors for adenosine, the signal that tells the brain it is tired. If caffeine is still active at bedtime, deep slow-wave sleep is measurably reduced.

bonus.short: Supplements: L-Theanine can smooth out jitters.
bonus.detail: L-Theanine raises alpha brain wave activity, and some people take it with caffeine to take the edge off. The evidence is mixed, so treat it as optional rather than established.

essential.short: Hydration: Water first, then coffee.
essential.detail: After sleep-deprived nights, the body wakes in a state of mild dehydration. Water and a balanced breakfast resolve the underlying physiological deficit that caffeine merely masks.

bonus.short: Timing: Delaying the first coffee is popular but unproven.
bonus.detail: The cortisol wake-up rise peaks about 30 to 45 minutes after waking. No trial shows that coffee in that window blunts it or causes dependence. Dependence comes from regular daily use, not from the timing of the first cup.

risks: Insomnia from delayed clearance
Anxiety and jitters
Frequent urination (mild diuretic effect)
caffeine.visualizer_note: Low overall harm; mainly disrupts sleep with mild cardiac strain. Fatal overdose needs extreme doses (grams).

2cb.name: 2C-B

Oral.note: Extremely steep dose-response curve. Use a milligram scale. Never estimate by eye.

Insufflated.note: Extremely painful to insufflate. Not recommended.

2cb.sleep_strategy: Shorter than LSD. Standard recovery protocol sufficient.

essential.short: Dose: Use a milligram scale. A 2 mg difference is significant.
essential.detail: 2C-B has an exceptionally steep dose-response curve. Around 5–15 mg it is largely entactogenic; above about 15 mg the psychedelic effects come forward, and above about 25 mg they can be overwhelming. A difference of 2–3 mg can turn a manageable state into a crisis. Never estimate by sight. The most accurate method is volumetric dosing, where you dissolve a precisely weighed amount in a known volume of liquid.

essential.short: ⚠️ Test it: "pink cocaine" / Tusi is usually NOT 2C-B.
essential.detail: Powders and pills sold as 2C-B are often something else. 'Tusi', 'tuci' or 'pink cocaine' in particular rarely contains 2C-B and is typically a ketamine and MDMA mixture, sometimes with caffeine. Drug-checking has repeatedly found 2C-B tablets contaminated with 2C-H, a leftover precursor that can block MAO-B and make a dose hit harder and less predictably. Use a reagent test or a drug-checking service before dosing.

essential.short: Stomach: Empty stomach reduces nausea.
essential.detail: 2C-B is known for intense gastrointestinal distress during onset. An empty stomach minimizes nausea and reduces the likelihood of vomiting during the come-up phase.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): ginger (250–500 mg) can help with nausea.
bonus.detail: Ginger 30 minutes beforehand may ease nausea. Lab work suggests it blocks the same gut serotonin receptor that anti-sickness drugs target, but that has not been confirmed in people.

essential.short: Onset: Avoid food or heavy liquids for 60–90 minutes.
essential.detail: The onset phase produces intense stomach cramping and nausea. Consuming any solid food or heavy liquids during this window dramatically increases the probability of vomiting.

essential.short: Hydration: Standard electrolyte protocol after nausea passes.
essential.detail: Once peak effects are established and the nausea passes, go back to the baseline hydration plan: water with electrolytes at a comfortable pace.

bonus.short: Note: Visuals can be intense while headspace stays relatively clear.
bonus.detail: Unlike LSD or psilocybin, 2C-B typically produces vivid visual effects while maintaining a relatively lucid mental state. Understanding this pattern helps prevent anxiety.

essential.short: Recovery: a normal meal. Some people add magnesium.
essential.detail: 2C-B mimics serotonin at the receptor site rather than forcing massive endogenous release (like MDMA). The neurological comedown is significantly milder.

bonus.short: Note: No 5-HTP needed (no serotonin depletion).
bonus.detail: Unlike MDMA, 2C-B does not deplete serotonin stores. The aggressive supplementation protocol for MDMA comedowns is unnecessary for 2C-B recovery.

essential.short: Mood: Usually a mild positive afterglow.
essential.detail: Most people report a gentle, positive mood the day after 2C-B, unlike the depletion that follows MDMA or amphetamine.

bonus.short: Routine: Standard recovery. Hydrate, eat and get sunlight.
bonus.detail: No special supplements or interventions are needed. Follow the sober baseline: hydrate, eat a balanced breakfast, and get sunlight exposure.

risks: Nausea and vomiting during onset
Dosing errors: a steep dose curve, and redosing before the first dose arrives
Frequently mis-sold ('pink cocaine' is rarely 2C-B)
Agitation, confusion, panic and a fast pulse at higher doses
2cb.visualizer_note: Generally low harm at correct doses, but a steep dose-response and frequent mis-selling ('pink cocaine') drive the risk.

4mmc.name: 4-MMC (Mephedrone)

Insufflated.note: Snorted doses are far lower than oral. 4-MMC is very compulsive, so some people choose to pre-measure a total limit for the session.

4mmc.sleep_strategy: Very difficult. Stop redosing hours before planned sleep.

essential.short: Control: Because 4-MMC's peak is short and compulsive, many people find it helps to pre-measure a set amount and leave the rest at home.
essential.detail: The main danger of 4-MMC is how strongly it drives you to redose. The euphoric peak fades within 45–60 minutes, leaving an overwhelming urge to take more. Physical limits, such as only carrying a pre-measured amount, are the most effective way to manage this.

essential.short: ⚠️ Identity: "4-MMC" is now frequently a different cathinone. Test it.
essential.detail: European drug-checking services repeatedly find powder sold as 4-MMC or 3-MMC that contains no mephedrone at all, commonly 3-CMC, 4-CMC or N-ethylpentedrone. These are barely researched, strongly compulsive, and in some cases linked to deaths. Appearance and smell are no guide, so use a drug-checking service where available.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): some people pre-load antioxidants (ALA, vitamin C); neuroprotection is unproven in humans.
bonus.detail: Cathinones can generate oxidative stress, so a buffer is plausible, but animal results conflict and there is no human data. Pre-loading antioxidants provides some neuroprotective buffer against free radical damage.

during.focus: Temperature monitoring and resisting compulsive redosing.

essential.short: Heat: Keep an eye on your temperature and cool down regularly.
essential.detail: 4-MMC triggers extreme hyperthermia and tachycardia simultaneously. Core body temperature is worth watching. Taking breaks in ventilated areas helps keep it down.

essential.short: ⚠️ Heart: stop and get help for chest pain or a pounding, irregular heartbeat. Cold blue fingers are an earlier sign.
essential.detail: 4-MMC strongly narrows blood vessels in the fingers, toes and other extremities. Cold, blue or numb extremities are warning signs of dangerous strain on your circulation.

essential.short: Avoid mixing with alcohol (may worsen neurotoxicity).
essential.detail: Animal studies suggest that combining 4-MMC with alcohol may increase oxidative stress and nerve damage, but this has not been confirmed in humans. The combination also masks how intoxicated you are, which encourages heavier use of both, and adds strain to the heart.

sources.label: Ciudad-Roberts et al. 2016: Ethanol + mephedrone neurotoxicity (mice)

essential.short: Crash: Severe. Both dopamine and serotonin are depleted.
essential.detail: 4-MMC depletes both serotonin and dopamine at once, producing severe lethargy, acute anxiety, paranoia and deep low mood. This is one of the harshest comedowns of any common recreational drug.

essential.short: Environment: Safe, calm space for comedown.
essential.detail: The psychological crash can be extreme, bringing anxiety, paranoia and low mood. A dark, quiet, cool space with people you trust makes it noticeably easier.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): antioxidants and magnesium.
bonus.detail: There is no human evidence that vitamin C or ALA repair stimulant damage. Magnesium may ease jaw and muscle tension, but it does not act on narrowed blood vessels.

essential.short: Mood: Expect severe depression and anxiety (2–4 days).
essential.detail: The dual depletion of serotonin and dopamine produces one of the most severe comedowns of any recreational substance. This is temporary but can last 2–4 days.

bonus.short: Recovery (optional): balanced meals; some people take 5-HTP (only 24+ hours later) and L-Tyrosine.
bonus.detail: 5-HTP is a serotonin precursor and L-tyrosine a dopamine precursor, but neither has been shown in people to speed recovery. Food helps generally rather than specifically: carbohydrate is what helps tryptophan reach the brain, while protein competes with it.

risks: Compulsive redosing (extremely addictive pattern)
Severe peripheral vasoconstriction
Dangerous cardiac stress (fast or irregular heartbeat, chest pain)
Overheating, worse when dancing in a hot room
Neurotoxicity (worsened by alcohol in animal studies)
Serotonin syndrome if mixed with MAOIs, or with MDMA and other serotonergic drugs
4mmc.visualizer_note: Very high cardiac strain and compulsive redosing; deaths have occurred, and mis-selling as unknown cathinones adds risk.

cmc.name: 3-CMC / 4-CMC

Insufflated.note: 3-CMC figures. The tiers are user-reported, not clinical, and PsychonautWiki advises against snorting. A batch may be 4-CMC or a mix, which is less studied and probably more serotonergic, so treat anything sold as 'CMC, 3-MMC or mephedrone' as a low test dose.

Oral.note: 3-CMC figures (PsychonautWiki and SaferParty broadly agree). Approximate and user-derived; 4-CMC tiers are not established.

cmc.sleep_strategy: Sleep is difficult while active, and compulsive redosing tends to stretch the night. Stop redosing several hours before you want to sleep.

essential.short: ⚠️ Identity: powder sold as 3-MMC, mephedrone, MDMA, speed or ketamine is often 3-CMC or 4-CMC, so get it checked if you can.
essential.detail: Drug-checking services keep finding CMC where another drug was expected (Vienna, Feb 2025: all three "3-MMC" samples were pure 3-CMC; Berlin, 2026: a "3-MMC" that was 88.9% 4-CMC). Look and smell tell you nothing about which cathinone it is or how strong it is.

essential.short: Start low: the dose numbers are rough, so take a small test dose and wait.
essential.detail: The published tiers come from user reports rather than studies, and 4-CMC is barely characterised, so a small test dose is the only reliable way to read an unknown batch before committing to a full dose.

essential.short: Control: because the peak is short and pushes for a repeat, many people weigh out a session limit and leave the rest at home.
essential.detail: Like mephedrone, CMC's euphoria fades within the hour and drives a strong urge to redose. Carrying only a pre-measured amount is the most reliable brake on a compulsive night.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): some people pre-load antioxidants (vitamin C, ALA); neuroprotection is unproven in humans.
bonus.detail: Cathinones generate oxidative stress, so an antioxidant buffer is plausible, but it has not been demonstrated in people and does not replace limiting dose and spacing use.

during.focus: Pace redosing; watch your heart and temperature.

essential.short: Redosing: space it out and respect your pre-set limit. This is where CMC bites.
essential.detail: The short peak invites a bump every 20–60 minutes; each redose stacks cardiovascular strain and vasoconstriction and deepens the eventual comedown.

essential.short: Heart: cold, numb or blue fingers, chest tightness, or a pounding/irregular heartbeat mean it's time to stop and cool down.
essential.detail: Case reports describe tachycardia, extra beats and chest pain, and the peripheral vasoconstriction gets worse with each redose.

essential.short: ⚠️ Depressants: be very careful stacking CMC on GHB/GBL, ketamine, benzodiazepines or opioids, because the stimulation hides how sedated you are.
essential.detail: When the stimulant fades first, the depressant can surface as sudden over-sedation or slowed breathing. Most confirmed 3-CMC deaths also involved alcohol, opioids or benzodiazepines.

essential.short: ⚠️ Serotonergic drugs: avoid stacking MDMA or meth, and don't combine with SSRIs or MAOIs.
essential.detail: CMC releases serotonin, 4-CMC especially, so adding other serotonergic drugs risks serotonin syndrome, and an MAOI can turn a normal dose dangerous.

bonus.short: Alcohol: mixing mainly masks how much you've taken and adds strain.
bonus.detail: It blunts your read on intoxication, encourages heavier use of both, and adds cardiac and dehydration load.

bonus.short: Hydration: sip water and take cool breaks, but you do not need litres.
bonus.detail: Stimulation, dancing and jaw-clenching drive heat and fluid loss; steady sips plus rest manage it without risking overhydration.

essential.short: Sleep: give yourself several hours between the last dose and trying to sleep.
essential.detail: It is a strong, fairly short stimulant, but redosing stretches wakefulness and insomnia is a common after-effect.

essential.short: Comedown: expect a flat, anxious, sometimes paranoid mood. It passes.
essential.detail: Low mood, anxiety, listlessness and sometimes confusion are common as it wears off, though the cause is not established, occasionally brief paranoia; a calm, safe space with trusted people helps most.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): magnesium and antioxidants are sometimes used; benefits are modest.
bonus.detail: Magnesium may ease jaw tension and vasoconstriction, and antioxidants target oxidative stress.

essential.short: Mood: a low, anxious mood for a day or two is the neurotransmitter rebound, not your baseline.
essential.detail: Mood usually lifts over a day or two with food, fluids and sleep; if low mood drags on, a longer break and some support are worth considering.
