bonus.short: Recovery (optional): eat properly and rehydrate; if you use 5-HTP, wait at least 24 h after the last dose.
bonus.detail: Precursors and balanced meals support recovery, but 5-HTP too soon after a serotonin-releasing drug is best avoided.

risks: Often mis-sold. Powder sold as 'CMC, 3-MMC, mephedrone, MDMA or speed' frequently contains a different or unknown cathinone at an unknown dose
Strong compulsive redosing (a short peak drives a hard urge to repeat)
Cardiac strain: tachycardia, arrhythmias, chest pain, severe vasoconstriction
Suspected high neurotoxicity (animal and structural evidence; unconfirmed in humans)
Agitation, confusion, psychosis and seizures during use; harsh anxious or paranoid comedown after
Life-threatening serotonin syndrome if mixed with MDMA, meth, SSRIs, MAOIs or 5-HTP
cmc.visualizer_note: A barely researched mephedrone stand-in that is frequently not what the label says. The real dangers are a strong pull to keep redosing, suspected nerve damage and strain on the heart, plus a harsh, anxious comedown. Deaths have occurred, sometimes alongside other drugs and sometimes from 3-CMC itself.

ghb.name: GHB

Oral.note: ⚠️ These volumes assume a GHB solution. Street solutions vary a lot in strength (anywhere from about 200 to 1000 mg/mL), so a volume alone is never a reliable dose. Always start with a small test dose from a new batch or source. GBL is a different substance with much smaller doses; it has its own profile.

ghb.sleep_strategy: Sleep arrives suddenly, so have a sober companion and lie on your side. If a person cannot be woken, that is overdose, not sleep: call an ambulance and keep them on their side while you wait.

essential.short: ⚠️ CRITICAL DANGER: GHB/GBL has an EXTREMELY NARROW therapeutic window. The difference between a recreational dose and a fatal overdose is often a single milliliter or less.
essential.detail: GHB/GBL is a CNS depressant with a margin measured in drops. Loss of consciousness occurs from ~3 grams, but purity varies so dramatically (roughly 200 to 1000 mg/mL) that visual estimation is effectively impossible. A dose that feels like 1 mL might actually contain 200 mg or 600 mg. This is not a substance to experiment with.

essential.short: ⚠️ Never use with alcohol or any other depressants (benzodiazepines, opioids, pregabalin, ketamine, etc.).
essential.detail: GHB combined with other CNS depressants causes catastrophic respiratory depression. Even small GHB doses + alcohol → unconsciousness. If vomiting occurs while unconscious, aspiration (choking) is likely fatal. Alcohol makes this far more likely, but GHB alone still causes the largest single share of deaths.

essential.short: Measurement: Use a calibrated vial or syringe. Never eyeball. Start low with any new batch.
essential.detail: The only harm reduction approach is strict measurement discipline. Visual estimation fails with GHB. Use a marked syringe (0.1 mL precision) and always start conservatively with a new batch to assess its actual concentration.

essential.short: ⚠️ GHB is not GBL: GBL is a separate, stronger substance with its own profile.
essential.detail: GBL turns into GHB in the body, but by volume it is roughly 2 to 3 times stronger and faster-acting, so the same millilitres can be a 2 to 3 times overdose. This table is for GHB only, so use the dedicated GBL profile for GBL. If you do not know whether a liquid is GHB or GBL, treat it as GBL and start very low.

essential.short: ⚠️ Overdose signs → CALL EMERGENCY IMMEDIATELY: Loss of consciousness, irregular or stopped breathing, choking, seizure-like movements.
essential.detail: A GHB overdose shows up as sudden unconsciousness and slowed breathing. Because the drug suppresses the gag reflex, vomiting while unconscious is silent and goes into the lungs. This is fatal without immediate medical help. Call emergency services (112) at once if someone stops responding or their breathing becomes irregular.

essential.short: ⚠️ NO REDOSING if subjective effects fade. Effects wear off while GHB is still in the bloodstream.
essential.detail: GHB subjective effects dissipate within 2–3 hours, but the drug remains active in the blood much longer. GHB clearance saturates at higher doses, so a second dose can push blood levels far above the first → overdose. This is the pattern leading to most GHB hospitalizations.

essential.short: ⚠️ Sober companion: someone must stay awake, sober and watching.
essential.detail: A sober person must remain conscious and aware of everyone using GHB. They need to: monitor breathing, prevent additional doses, watch for overdose signs, and call emergency services if anything seems wrong. Never use GHB alone or without a completely sober, trained watcher.

bonus.short: Hydration: Non-alcoholic beverages only. Max 0.5L/hour.
bonus.detail: Drinking fast while dancing can dilute blood sodium (hyponatremia), so keep hydration moderate. checkit! advises no more than half a litre of non-alcoholic drink per hour.

essential.short: ⚠️ Sleep can hit suddenly, so lie on your side before it does. If someone cannot be woken, that is overdose, not sleep: call an ambulance.
essential.detail: Sleep on GHB often arrives suddenly and involuntarily, so people pass out despite meaning to stay awake. Make sure you are in the recovery position, on your left side, so that if you vomit, gravity keeps it out of your lungs.

essential.short: ⚠️ If regular use: Dependence can develop after just weeks.
essential.detail: Physical and psychological dependence develops rapidly with repeated GHB use. Withdrawal is severe: anxiety, panic, insomnia (persisting for days), trembling, nausea, delirium with hallucinations. Withdrawal MUST occur under medical supervision. Do not attempt to quit suddenly.

essential.short: Recovery: Electrolytes and normal nutrition.
essential.detail: GHB leaves the system relatively quickly, but sleep disruption and the intensity of the experience create fatigue. Rehydrate with electrolyte drinks and resume normal eating.

risks: EXTREMELY narrow dose window, so overdose is possible with only a small increase in dose
Respiratory arrest and death (especially with alcohol or depressants)
Choking/aspiration during unconsciousness
Sudden involuntary sleep onset
Rapid dependence (physical and psychological)
Severe withdrawal requiring medical supervision
Memory loss (anterograde amnesia)
ghb.visualizer_note: The low 'strain' bars hide the real danger: an extremely narrow dose window and overdose that stops your breathing, especially with alcohol.

gbl.name: GBL

Oral.note: ⚠️ Never reuse a GHB dose for GBL. GBL is about 2 to 3 times stronger by volume (1 mL is roughly 1.66 g of GHB salt) and hits faster, in 3 to 10 minutes. Above about 2 mL it can drop you into sudden deep sleep. Always dilute it in a soft drink, because neat GBL burns, measure with a 0.1 mL syringe, and start with a small test dose from a new batch.

gbl.sleep_strategy: Sleep arrives suddenly and involuntarily, even faster than with GHB. Never use GBL without a sober companion, and use the recovery position.

essential.short: ⚠️ GBL is NOT GHB: it is ~2–3× stronger by volume and hits in minutes.
essential.detail: GBL is a precursor the body rapidly converts to GHB. By volume it is roughly 2–3× stronger and faster-acting (1 mL ≈ 1.66 g GHB salt), so a volume that is a common GHB dose can be a serious GBL overdose. Never carry over GHB dosing. If you are unsure which liquid you have, treat it as GBL and start very low.

essential.short: ⚠️ CRITICAL: The margin between a normal dose and an overdose is tiny, often under 0.5 mL.
essential.detail: GBL is a CNS depressant with an extremely narrow window. Because it is so concentrated, a difference of a fraction of a millilitre matters: loss of consciousness and respiratory depression can follow a small increase in dose. This is not a substance to estimate by eye.

essential.short: ⚠️ Never use with alcohol, ketamine, or any depressant (benzodiazepines, opioids, pregabalin).
essential.detail: GBL (as GHB) combined with other CNS depressants causes catastrophic respiratory depression. Even small amounts with alcohol can cause unconsciousness; vomiting while unconscious leads to fatal aspiration. This combination is the leading cause of GHB/GBL deaths.

essential.short: Dilute it: mix a measured dose into a soft drink and drink it straight away. Never swallow GBL neat.
essential.detail: Undiluted GBL is caustic and can burn the mouth, throat and stomach. Always dilute a measured dose in a non-alcoholic soft drink, measure with a 0.1 mL syringe, keep a written note of what you took and when, and start low with any new batch.

essential.short: ⚠️ Overdose signs → CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY: cannot be woken, irregular or stopped breathing, choking, seizure-like movements.
essential.detail: A GBL overdose causes sudden unconsciousness and slowed breathing. Because it suppresses the gag reflex, vomiting while unconscious is silent and goes into the lungs, which is fatal without immediate help. Put the person in the recovery position and call emergency services the moment their breathing becomes irregular or they cannot be woken.

essential.short: ⚠️ NO REDOSING when effects fade. GBL is still in your blood.
essential.detail: Subjective effects fade within 1–2 hours, but the drug is still active. Taking another dose stacks on top of the first and pushes total blood levels toward overdose. Waiting out the urge is essential; many GBL/GHB hospitalisations follow redosing too soon.

essential.short: ⚠️ Sober companion: someone must stay awake, sober and watching your breathing.
essential.detail: A completely sober person must watch everyone using GBL: monitor their breathing, stop extra doses, watch for overdose signs, and call 112 if anything seems wrong. Never use GBL alone.

bonus.short: Hydration: non-alcoholic drinks only, max ~0.5 L/hour.
bonus.detail: Keep hydration moderate and strictly non-alcoholic. Over-hydration adds little benefit and any alcohol is dangerous with GBL.

essential.short: ⚠️ Expect sudden, involuntary sleep, so use the recovery position, on your side.
essential.detail: Sleep onset on GBL is often abrupt and unavoidable. Lie on your side so that if vomiting occurs, gravity keeps the airway clear. A sober person should keep watching breathing until you are fully alert.

essential.short: ⚠️ Dependence forms fast: daily use can cause dependence within weeks.
essential.detail: Regular, especially daily, GBL or GHB use causes rapid physical dependence. Withdrawal is severe, bringing anxiety, panic, insomnia for days, trembling, nausea and delirium with hallucinations, and it must be managed under medical supervision. Do not stop abruptly after a period of frequent use.

essential.short: Recovery: rehydrate and eat normally once fully alert.
essential.detail: GBL leaves the body quickly, but disrupted sleep and the intensity of the experience cause fatigue. Rehydrate with electrolyte drinks and resume normal eating once you are fully awake and oriented.

risks: EXTREMELY narrow dose window, so a fraction of a millilitre can cause an overdose
Faster onset and higher strength than GHB, so it is easy to misjudge
Respiratory arrest and death (especially with alcohol or depressants)
Choking/aspiration during sudden unconsciousness
Caustic if taken undiluted (burns mouth/throat)
Redosing too soon, sometimes with no memory of the first dose, stacking toward overdose
gbl.visualizer_note: The same lethal profile as GHB but harder to dose, being stronger by volume and faster in onset. The narrow dose window and overdose risk are the headline. GHB's expert harm score does not transfer to GBL, which that study never assessed.

benzodiazepines.name: Benzodiazepines

Oral.note: ⚠️ These numbers are diazepam equivalents, and the timeline shown is diazepam's too, both from PsychonautWiki's diazepam guide. Other benzos run far shorter or far longer, so a designer benzo can leave you impaired well past the window shown. Benzos differ hugely in strength: about 0.5 mg of alprazolam (Xanax) or 0.5 mg of clonazepam equals about 10 mg of diazepam, roughly 20 times stronger by weight, and about 1 mg of lorazepam or etizolam equals about 10 mg of diazepam. Convert your own drug before dosing, for example with the Ashton table at benzo.org.uk, though designer benzos like etizolam are not listed there, so use PsychonautWiki or TripSit for those. Counterfeit pressed pills sold as 'Xanax' or 'Valium' routinely contain unknown, variable or far stronger designer benzos such as bromazolam, or even nitazene opioids, so the dose is a guess. Get them drug-checked and start with a fraction, such as half, then wait at least an hour.

benzodiazepines.sleep_strategy: Benzodiazepines induce sedation and sleep, but degrade sleep quality (less deep/REM sleep), and long-acting ones like diazepam leave next-day grogginess for 12–36 h. Never stack other depressants (alcohol, opioids, GHB) to get to sleep. Place anyone heavily sedated in the recovery position and monitor breathing.

essential.short: ⚠️ Depressant combinations: Do not combine with opioids, alcohol, GHB/GBL, or other depressants.
essential.detail: Benzodiazepines are fairly safe on their own (wide therapeutic index), but combined with any other CNS depressant they potentiate sedation and respiratory depression, leading to sudden unconsciousness, aspiration and death. Benzo-plus-depressant combinations are one of the leading drivers of overdose deaths. Even a moderate amount of alcohol or a small opioid dose can tip this over.

essential.short: ⚠️ Counterfeit pills: A pressed 'Xanax' or 'Valium' is often not what the imprint says, so get it drug-checked and start with a fraction.
essential.detail: Street and pressed benzo pills are unpredictable in content and strength. Tablets sold as diazepam or alprazolam frequently contain a different, stronger designer benzodiazepine such as bromazolam or phenazolam, or, increasingly in Europe, a nitazene opioid substituted into the benzo market. The imprint, colour and blister pack prove nothing. Because the real dose is a guess, use a drug-checking service where available and start with a small fraction of a pill.

sources.label: Correlation / TEDI: European Drug Checking Trends 2018–2024
EUDA: New psychoactive substances (European Drug Report 2025)

essential.short: Dose in diazepam-equivalents and start low: potency varies 20x between common benzos, and far more for designer ones.
essential.detail: Roughly 0.5 mg alprazolam or clonazepam, or 1 mg lorazepam or etizolam, is equivalent to 10 mg diazepam. Confusing milligrams between benzos is a common way to massively overshoot. Convert your specific drug to diazepam-equivalents first, and remember these are estimates that vary between individuals and reference tables.

essential.short: Go slow and not alone: take a fraction with someone sober nearby, then wait at least an hour before considering more.
essential.detail: Oral onset is around 20–40 minutes. The classic trap is redosing during that delay, and then the amnesia sets in and further pills get taken without any memory of them, stacking into a blackout or overdose. One dose, then wait.

bonus.short: Not a routine comedown crutch: tolerance builds within days and dependence forms quickly with regular use.
bonus.detail: Using benzos to blunt a stimulant comedown or to sleep after events, if repeated, builds tolerance and physical dependence quickly. The stimulant also hides how sedated you are, so when it fades first the full benzo effect lands at once. Keeping benzo use occasional and spaced out is the main way to avoid a dependence that is difficult and dangerous to reverse.

bonus.short: Do not drive or operate machinery while dosed or the next day.
bonus.detail: Benzodiazepines impair coordination, reaction time and alertness, and long-acting ones leave residual impairment into the following day even when you feel fine.

during.focus: Avoiding depressant stacking and blackout-driven redosing.

essential.short: ⚠️ Overdose signs: heavy sedation, slow or shallow breathing, unresponsiveness, blue lips. Put them in the recovery position and call 112.
essential.detail: Benzodiazepines alone rarely stop breathing, but combined with other depressants, or when a pill secretly contains a nitazene opioid, they cause life-threatening slowing of the breath. If someone cannot be roused, is breathing slowly or shallowly, or has blue lips or fingertips, put them on their side in the recovery position and call emergency services. If an opioid may be involved, give naloxone if you have it. Naloxone does not reverse the benzo itself, but it reverses the opioid that may be the real danger. One dose may not be enough: a nitazene can outlast it, so stay with them, give another if their breathing slows again, and call 112 either way.

sources.label: EUDA: New psychoactive substances (nitazenes in the benzo market)

essential.short: ⚠️ Do not add alcohol, opioids or GHB/GBL on top while dosed.
essential.detail: Topping up with another depressant while a benzo is active is when sudden, unexpected loss of consciousness happens, with a real risk of choking on vomit. The two substances strengthen each other strongly and unpredictably.

essential.short: Blackouts and disinhibition: stay with trusted people; don't make big decisions or redose.
essential.detail: Benzodiazepines commonly cause anterograde amnesia, meaning you stop forming memories, along with disinhibition and, at higher doses, a false sense of being sober while badly impaired. This drives risky behaviour and repeat doses that are not remembered. Staying around people you trust and keeping the pills out of reach once you have dosed protects against this.

bonus.short: Anyone who passes out goes on their side in the recovery position, monitored.
bonus.detail: A sedated person's gag reflex is suppressed, so vomit aspiration is the practical killer. The recovery position keeps the airway clear; never leave a heavily sedated person alone.

essential.short: ⚠️ Don't chase sleep with more depressants.
essential.detail: A long-acting benzo like diazepam is still active for many hours. Adding alcohol, opioids or z-drugs on top to get to sleep re-creates the dangerous depressant stack overnight, when no one is watching your breathing.

essential.short: Residual impairment lingers: diazepam's long half-life means grogginess for 12–36 h, so do not drive.
essential.detail: After-effects and impaired coordination persist well beyond the main experience, especially for long-half-life benzos (diazepam's half-life with active metabolites can reach several days). You can be legally and functionally impaired the next morning while feeling recovered.

bonus.short: Keep monitoring anyone heavily sedated; recovery position until fully alert.
bonus.detail: Sedation can deepen after the last dose as absorption continues. Keep a sedated person on their side and checked on until they are clearly awake and oriented.

essential.short: ⚠️ If you have been using regularly, never stop abruptly. Taper under medical supervision.
essential.detail: Physical dependence forms quickly. In someone dependent, stopping suddenly can cause seizures and delirium that are genuinely life-threatening. The safe route is a gradual dose reduction guided by a doctor. This is one of the few withdrawals, alongside alcohol, that can kill.

essential.short: Space out use and keep breaks: tolerance and dependence build within days.
essential.detail: Tolerance to the sedative effects develops within a couple of days of continuous use and returns to baseline over about 7–14 days of abstinence. Keeping clear gaps between uses is what prevents a dependence taking hold.

bonus.short: Expect rebound anxiety or poor sleep the next day, and do not re-dose to fix it.
bonus.detail: As the drug clears, anxiety and insomnia can rebound above baseline. Taking another dose to relieve this is exactly how a dependence cycle starts; ride it out if you can.

risks: Fatal respiratory depression when combined with opioids, alcohol, GHB/GBL or other depressants (a leading overdose driver)
Counterfeit pills (fake Xanax or Valium) may contain stronger designer benzos such as bromazolam, or nitazene opioids, so the dose is a guess
Rapid dependence; abrupt withdrawal can cause life-threatening seizures and delirium (taper, never stop suddenly)
Choking on vomit while unconscious, because sedation blocks the gag reflex
Blackouts and anterograde amnesia
Disinhibition and risky behaviour

Tolerance develops within days

benzodiazepines.visualizer_note: On their own, benzodiazepines have a wide safety margin, but they are a leading driver of overdose deaths when stacked with opioids, alcohol or GHB, and counterfeit pills can hide nitazene opioids. The everyday harms are fast dependence, dangerous withdrawal, and blackout-driven redosing.

heroin.name: Heroin (Diamorphine)

Smoked.note: ⚠️ These numbers are deliberately conservative, not a measurement of what is in your bag. Street purity runs from about 10 to over 70 percent and swings between batches, so the same weight can be a very different dose. Always start with a tiny test dose from a new bag. For reference, in someone with no tolerance about 30 mg of pure diamorphine injected can be lethal, and about 60 mg of pure heroin is the commonly cited lethal dose.

Insufflated.note: ⚠️ These numbers are deliberately conservative, not a measurement of what is in your bag, and purity swings between batches. Always start with a tiny test dose from a new bag. Snorting damages the nasal lining and septum, so use your own rounded-tip tube and rinse your nose after use.

heroin.sleep_strategy: Heroin induces sedation and sleep. Place the person in recovery position to prevent aspiration. Never leave someone nodding off unmonitored.

essential.short: ⚠️ LETHAL OVERDOSE RISK: Street purity varies 10–72%. Any new batch, source, or period of abstinence (even 2 days) dramatically changes overdose threshold.
essential.detail: Heroin purity is wildly inconsistent. German street samples averaged about 18.7% in 2021 and ranged from 10 to 72%, and the mix changes from batch to batch. Pharmaceutical diamorphine is near-pure and several times stronger by weight than typical street heroin. After even a brief break of 2–5 days, opioid tolerance falls sharply, and going back to a previous dose after a break is one of the most common causes of fatal heroin overdose. The sharpest windows are the first weeks after prison, hospital, detox or stopping substitution treatment. Coming out of any of those, dose far lower than before and carry naloxone.

essential.short: ⚠️ Contamination: Street heroin may contain fentanyl or nitazenes. Test it; carry extra naloxone.
essential.detail: Synthetic opioids, fentanyl and especially nitazenes, increasingly turn up in the European heroin supply and are far stronger than heroin itself. They are a leading driver of recent overdose deaths across several EU countries. Fentanyl strips do not detect nitazenes at all, and they miss some fentanyl analogues too, so a clean strip does not mean the bag is safe. Nitazene strips are sold separately but are hard to get in most places. Because these opioids are potent and can outlast a single naloxone dose, carry several doses and be ready to give another.

sources.label: Fentanyl test strips vs 251 synthetic opioids (2023)

essential.short: ⚠️ Never use alone. Have naloxone (Narcan) available and ensure companions know how to use it.
essential.detail: Naloxone blocks opioids and brings breathing back. The nasal spray takes about 2 to 3 minutes, not seconds. If nothing changes after 2 to 3 minutes, give a second device in the other nostril. It does almost nothing to someone who has not taken opioids, so if you are unsure what they took, give it anyway. To give it: lay them on their back, tilt the head back, put the nozzle in one nostril and press the plunger hard. Do not test-spray it first, each device holds a single dose. Everyone present should know the signs of overdose (blue lips, slow or stopped breathing, unresponsiveness). Supervised consumption rooms are the safest place where they exist. If you will be alone anyway: take less than usual, leave the door unlocked, tell someone to call you at a set time, and use an overdose prevention phone line if one covers your country.

essential.short: ⚠️ Never combine with alcohol, benzodiazepines, pregabalin or gabapentin, GHB/GBL, ketamine, or other depressants.
essential.detail: Combining opioids with any other CNS depressant causes synergistic respiratory depression that rapidly leads to unconsciousness, aspiration, and death. Mixing depressants is one of the most common ways opioid users die. Pregabalin and gabapentin count here too, and are easy to miss because they are prescribed for nerve pain and anxiety. Even small amounts of alcohol with heroin can be fatal.

essential.short: Test dose: Always start with a tiny amount from any new batch.
essential.detail: Use drug-checking services where available. With any new source or batch, start with a fraction of what you would normally use, then wait for the full effect before taking more. Smoked and snorted heroin peaks 30 to 90 minutes in, so topping up before that stacks two doses into one. Purity swings mean a dose that was safe last week may be lethal today. Do not rely on dosing advice from regular users, because their tolerance makes their doses lethal for anyone without it.

bonus.short: Route: Smoking (foil) is significantly safer than injection.
bonus.detail: Smoking produces a slower onset and lower peak blood concentration than injection, substantially reducing overdose risk. Injection carries additional risks: vein collapse, abscesses, endocarditis, and blood-borne infections (HIV, Hepatitis C). If injecting, the dose is far lower than smoked or snorted: with no tolerance about 5 to 10 mg of pure heroin. Never carry the numbers from the tiers above over to a needle. Use sterile equipment only and never share needles, water, or filters.

bonus.short: Smoking equipment: Use uncoated aluminium foil and personal tubes. Do not share.
bonus.detail: Sharing smoking tubes transmits Hepatitis C and herpes. Use only uncoated aluminium foil (food-grade). Each person should have their own tube with a smooth, rounded tip to prevent oral cuts.

essential.short: ⚠️ OVERDOSE: Blue lips/fingertips, slow or stopped breathing, unresponsiveness → CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY. Give naloxone if you have it, and breathe for them if their breathing is slow or stopped.
essential.detail: An opioid overdose kills by stopping the breathing, long before the heart stops. Breathing goes slow and shallow first: count for 15 seconds, and fewer than 3 breaths in that time (under 12 a minute) is already an emergency. It can fall to 2–4 a minute or stop. Blue-tinted cold skin, collapsing blood pressure, pinpoint pupils and unresponsiveness are emergency signs. Call emergency services first. Call even if you are scared of the police: on the phone you only have to describe the symptoms, you do not have to say drugs were involved. Then breathing comes first: tilt the head back, clear the mouth, and give naloxone nasal spray if you have it. If they breathe less than once every 5 seconds, give one rescue breath every 5 seconds. If they are not breathing at all, start CPR, 30 chest compressions to 2 breaths. Only once they breathe normally on their own, put them on their side. Naloxone lasts 30 to 90 minutes, less than heroin, so breathing can fail again and more doses may be needed. It also throws a dependent person straight into withdrawal: they may wake up sick and want to use again at once, which is how people go over a second time. Stay with them and keep watching the breathing until help arrives.

sources.label: AHA 2025 Guidelines: Adult Basic Life Support

essential.short: ⚠️ Speedball danger: Never combine heroin with cocaine or stimulants.
essential.detail: Stimulants increase respiration rate, masking the respiratory depression caused by opioids. When the stimulant wears off first, the full opioid dose may suddenly overwhelm the respiratory system, causing delayed fatal respiratory arrest. This combination causes extreme cardiovascular strain.

essential.short: ⚠️ Nausea: Vomiting is common. Anyone drowsy or nodding must lie on their side, never sit upright.
essential.detail: Heroin commonly causes nausea and vomiting, especially at higher doses or in opioid-naive users. If someone is sedated and vomiting, the suppressed gag reflex means aspiration (inhaling vomit) is a severe risk. Always ensure they are on their side in the recovery position.

bonus.short: Avoid operating machinery, driving, or swimming.
bonus.detail: Heroin severely impairs coordination, reaction time, and consciousness. The sedative effects can cause sudden loss of consciousness ("nodding") without warning.

essential.short: ⚠️ Recovery position: If sedated, place on their side. Monitor breathing continuously.
essential.detail: Opioid-induced sedation combined with nausea creates a high aspiration risk. The person must be placed on their side (recovery position) and breathing must be monitored continuously. Check them properly every few minutes: say their name loudly, shake the shoulders, then rub your knuckles hard on the breastbone. Deep snoring or gurgling is not sleep, it is a partly blocked airway and a classic overdose sign. If they do not react, treat it as an overdose. Never leave someone nodding off alone.

essential.short: ⚠️ Dependence: Physical dependence develops rapidly with regular use. Withdrawal begins 8–12 hours after last dose.
essential.detail: Regular multi-week use causes tolerance, requiring increased amounts. Withdrawal symptoms include sweating, chills, runny eyes/nose, vomiting, diarrhea, severe muscle cramps, insomnia, and extreme anxiety. Medical supervision for withdrawal is strongly recommended.

bonus.short: Hydration and light nutrition when alert.
bonus.detail: Once the person is alert and oriented, rehydrate with water or electrolyte drinks. Heroin suppresses appetite and causes constipation, so light, easily digestible meals support recovery.

essential.short: Do not redose to avoid withdrawal. Maintain consumption breaks of multiple days.
essential.detail: The wish to avoid withdrawal drives compulsive use. Each extra use deepens physical dependence. Keeping breaks of several days between uses lowers that risk, but only if you cut the dose when you come back. Tolerance drops off within 2 to 5 days, so after any break treat it like a first time and start at a small fraction of your old dose. This is only harm reduction: no pattern of heroin use is safe.

bonus.short: Recovery: Rehydrate, eat balanced meals, prioritise sleep.
bonus.detail: Heroin disrupts normal appetite, hydration, and bowel function. Fibre-rich foods help counter constipation. Rest and normal sleep cycles support physical recovery.

risks: Fatal respiratory depression (worse with other depressants; cocaine and other stimulants mask it, then it hits when they wear off)
Aspiration (choking on vomit while unconscious)
Extreme overdose risk after tolerance break (even 2 days)
Wildly variable street purity (10–72%)
Contamination with fentanyl or nitazenes (far stronger; may resist naloxone)
Rapid physical and psychological dependence
Severe withdrawal requiring medical supervision
Blood-borne infections from shared equipment (HIV, Hepatitis C)
heroin.visualizer_note: The strain bars look mild, but overdose that stops your breathing is the dominant, ever-present risk, made worse by lost tolerance and by fentanyl or nitazene contamination.

methamphetamine.name: Methamphetamine

Oral.note: Oral is the safest route. A full stomach delays absorption. Crystal purity averages about 98%, far stronger than street amphetamine.

Insufflated.note: Causes severe nasal mucosa damage. Use personal rounded-tip tubes. Do not share equipment.

Smoked.note: Smoking causes lung damage and elevated cancer risk. Rapid onset increases addiction potential.

methamphetamine.sleep_strategy: Sleep may be impossible for 12–30+ hours. Do not redose to delay the comedown. Plan adequate recovery time. Benzodiazepines should NOT be used as sleep aids without medical supervision.

essential.short: ⚠️ EXTREMELY HIGH ADDICTION POTENTIAL: Methamphetamine produces one of the strongest psychological dependencies of any recreational substance.
essential.detail: Methamphetamine triggers simultaneous massive release of dopamine, noradrenaline, and serotonin, producing intense euphoria that the brain rapidly becomes dependent on. Very high addiction potential with both psychological and physical withdrawal symptoms. Space sessions at least 4 weeks apart to reduce (but not eliminate) dependence risk.

essential.short: Crystal purity averages about 98%. This is NOT the same as street amphetamine (speed), so doses are far lower.
essential.detail: Crystal methamphetamine hydrochloride has a median purity of ~98.1%, compared to street amphetamine which is typically 10–30% pure. A dose of methamphetamine that looks similar to a speed dose can be 3–10× more pharmacologically active. Never apply amphetamine dosing knowledge to methamphetamine.

essential.short: Eat a balanced meal before use. Some people also take vitamins C and D and minerals (iron, calcium, magnesium).
essential.detail: Methamphetamine suppresses hunger, thirst, and pain perception for 6–30+ hours. The body continues to burn calories and deplete nutrients throughout. Pre-loading with balanced nutrition and supplements mitigates the severe nutritional depletion that contributes to the harsh comedown.

bonus.short: Use drug-checking services where available. Start with a small test dose.
bonus.detail: While crystal meth purity is typically high, adulterants and substitution do occur. Drug checking confirms identity and purity. Always start with a fraction of the intended dose from a new batch.

bonus.short: Plan your time: Set a hard stop time and recovery period before you start.
bonus.detail: The most dangerous pattern with methamphetamine is extending sessions to delay the comedown. Decide in advance when you will stop and ensure you have at least 24–48 hours of recovery time scheduled afterward.

during.focus: Cardiovascular monitoring, hydration, and preventing compulsive redosing.

essential.short: ⚠️ EMERGENCY: Chest pain, severe headache, seizures, extreme confusion, or body temperature >39°C → CALL 112 IMMEDIATELY.
essential.detail: Methamphetamine overdose can cause fatal pulmonary oedema, cerebral haemorrhage, cardiac arrhythmias, acute heart failure, and severe hyperthermia. These are medical emergencies requiring immediate intervention. Stroke and sudden cardiac death can occur even in young, healthy users.

essential.short: Do not redose. Methamphetamine lasts 6–30 hours. Redosing dramatically increases toxicity and addiction risk.
essential.detail: Methamphetamine is slowly metabolised by the body. Each redose adds to the total circulating dose without the previous amount being cleared. This compounds cardiovascular strain, neurotoxicity, and hyperthermia exponentially. The compulsion to redose is itself a primary danger.

essential.short: Hydration: Drink non-alcoholic fluids with electrolytes. Max 0.5L/hour.
essential.detail: Methamphetamine causes fluid loss through raised temperature, sweating and hours of activity, while blunting thirst. Drink steadily but avoid over-hydration. Electrolyte drinks replace sodium lost through sweating.

essential.short: ⚠️ Never combine with alcohol, because it masks overdose symptoms and causes severe strain on your organs.
essential.detail: Methamphetamine masks how drunk you feel, so people drink far past their usual limit. The combination causes extreme strain on the heart, liver toxicity, and a much higher risk of aggressive or violent behaviour. When the stimulant wears off, the full sedative load of the alcohol hits, risking slowed breathing and choking on vomit.

bonus.short: Take cooling breaks. Eat light foods and fruits even if not hungry.
bonus.detail: Methamphetamine elevates core body temperature and suppresses appetite. Active cooling (moving to ventilated areas, cold water on wrists) and forcing light meals maintain blood sugar and prevent dangerous hyperthermia.

bonus.short: ⚠️ Never mix with MAOI antidepressants (tranylcypromine, moclobemide, selegiline). Blood pressure can spike to stroke level. Bupropion and some SSRIs are a smaller concern but make effects stronger and longer.
bonus.detail: MAOIs block the breakdown of the noradrenaline methamphetamine releases, so blood pressure can climb to stroke level. This is the one combination every source ranks as life-threatening. Bupropion and some SSRIs such as fluoxetine and paroxetine block CYP2D6, one of the routes that clears methamphetamine, which makes effects stronger and longer rather than deadly. If you take any antidepressant, get medical advice first.

essential.short: Crash: Expect severe depression, exhaustion, irritability, and intense hunger (24–72 hours).
essential.detail: The methamphetamine comedown is one of the most severe of any stimulant. Massive dopamine depletion produces deep low mood, anxiety and exhaustion. Irritability, concentration problems and insomnia may last for days. This is temporary and will pass, so do not redose to manage it.

essential.short: Environment: Dark, quiet, safe space. Trusted companions.
essential.detail: Post-methamphetamine states can include paranoia, anxiety, and agitation. A calm, controlled environment with trusted people reduces psychological distress and prevents risky behaviour during the comedown.

bonus.short: Supplements (optional): balanced meals with protein and carbs; some people add vitamin C and magnesium.
bonus.detail: Vitamin C and magnesium support recovery: vitamin C for general antioxidant and nutrient replenishment (it does not meaningfully speed methamphetamine excretion, contrary to a common claim), and magnesium to counteract vasoconstriction and muscle tension. Protein-rich meals provide amino acid precursors for neurotransmitter replenishment.

essential.short: Recovery takes days, not hours. Using more stimulants to push through only deepens the crash, and rest is what helps.
essential.detail: The brain requires extended time to replenish depleted dopamine, noradrenaline, and serotonin stores. Using caffeine or other stimulants to push through the comedown delays recovery and compounds neurotoxicity. Plan for 24–48+ hours of rest and reduced function.

bonus.short: Mental health: Get help straight away for suicidal thoughts. Seek help if paranoia or anxiety last more than a few days.
bonus.detail: Methamphetamine use can trigger substance-induced psychosis including paranoia, delusions, and hallucinations. If psychiatric symptoms persist beyond the expected comedown window (2–4 days), this may indicate a more serious reaction requiring medical attention.

Severe hyperthermia
Substance-induced psychosis (paranoia, hallucinations)
One of the highest addiction potentials of any recreational substance
Extreme neurotoxicity and suspected irreversible brain changes
Severe comedown lasting 2–4 days (depression, anxiety, exhaustion)
